§ 1º O The conditional registration of a medicine can only be granted for products whose safety and efficacy have been evaluated, and it has been concluded that the benefits of its use outweigh the risks.
§ 2º O The conditional registration of a medicine can be revoked by Anvisa at any time, until its conversion into a full registration, in accordance with the regulations.
“Article 18. (Revoked)
§1. (Revoked)
.............................................................................................”(Amended)
Article 3. This law enters into force ninety days after its publication.
--- seg-1c94277027f9772c337adf8e [machine-unreviewed] ---
**Justification**

National drug control in Brazil is carried out by Anvisa, an agency with highly skilled professionals, structured to assess new registration requests and monitor this market.

It is important that regulations regarding the registration of pharmaceutical products be detailed and strict, but in some cases, citizens are harmed by the complex bureaucratic processes.

This bill aims to simplify certain aspects of drug registration legislation, allowing for faster processes in specific situations, without increasing risk or compromising patient effectiveness.

The proposal introduces "conditional drug registration," an accelerated registration procedure, only allowed in cases where a treatment for a condition with no effective alternatives emerges or in situations posing a risk to public health. This could benefit, for example, individuals with incurable diseases when new treatments become available, or during outbreaks of high-impact infectious diseases like the Zika virus.

Finally, we propose removing the requirement for foreign registration so that Anvisa can conduct the assessment. While this might have made sense in the past, Brazil's health surveillance system is already well-structured, allowing for analyses at a level comparable to more developed countries.

Previously established deadline, as provided in the regulations.
§1º O manufacturer will be notified of the procedure for evaluating a change in the duration of use validity, and may provide input during the process.
§2 If a change in validity is determined, the manufacturer will be informed, so that they can update the new deadline on the packaging.
Article 4 This law will enter into force one hundred and eighty days after its publication.

JUSTIFICATION
The validity period of medications is essential information that must be present on the packaging. Using treatments beyond the validity period may increase the risk of adverse effects and, primarily, reduce effectiveness.

However, studies have questioned the validity periods reported by the industry, suggesting that medications could be used for longer periods than indicated on the packaging.

For example, a study by the University of California analyzed a stock of medications stored for decades, with some exceeding 30-40 years past their validity. The results were surprising: twelve of the fourteen compounds evaluated remained as potent as when they were manufactured1. Another research, conducted in 2006, studied 122 different expired medications, with an average age of over four years. Two-thirds of these remained stable in each test performed.

Addressing this issue has the potential to generate significant savings. The U.S. Department of Defense, in partnership with the FDA, developed a program to manage the validity of its vast stock of medications reserved for disaster situations2. The extension of the validity period led, only in 2016, to a savings of two billion dollars that would have been wasted by destroying still-effective medications.

In Brazil, pharmaceutical manufacturers are currently responsible for informing the permitted use period of medications, but the choice of the deadline does not always follow scientific criteria. The pharmaceutical industry tends to opt for short deadlines to avoid future questions about effectiveness. The early expiration and disposal of medications can result in significant losses.

BILL NO. 10,171, OF 2018
(From Mr. Fábio Trad)
Amends Law No. 2,848, of December 7, 1940 - Penal Code, to establish the crime of illicit enrichment committed by a public official.
DISPOSITION:
ATTACH TO PL-5363/2005.
CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Plenary Consideration
THE NATIONAL CONGRESS decrees:
Article 1. This Law amends Law No. 2,848, of December 7, 1940 - Penal Code, to establish as a crime of illicit enrichment committed by a public official, when the public official has under his control, possession, and property, in a non-occasional manner, assets, rights, or values whose value is incompatible with his or her earnings obtained due to his or her office, employment, or public function.
Article 2. Add Article 312-A to Law No. 2,848, of December 7, 1940 - Penal Code, as follows:
Illicit Enrichment
Article 312-A. To have under his or her control, possession, or property, in a non-occasional manner, assets, rights, or values whose value is incompatible with his or her earnings obtained due to his or her office, employment, or public function:
Penalty - imprisonment from 4 (four) to 8 (eight) years and a fine.
§ 1. The same penalty applies if there is repayment or extinction of the public official's debts, even by a third party.
§ 2. The penalties are increased by one-half if the ownership or possession of the assets and values is fraudulently attributed to third parties.
Article 3. This Law enters into force on the date of its publication.
JUSTIFICATION
The illicit enrichment of a public official is indirect proof of corruption and related crimes, and particularly in Brazil, it has been reported almost daily by the media. In light of this well-known fact, we propose to present this Bill to consider as a crime under the Penal Code the illicit enrichment of a public official.
Thus, we propose to criminalize having under his or her control, possession, or property, in a non-occasional manner, assets, rights, or values whose value is incompatible with his or her earnings obtained due to his or her office, employment, or public function. Similarly, it is intended to punish with the same penalty if

===== PAGE 100 [page-80500449b20bc087cd516cc7] =====
--- seg-ddd8b0bd71958ab7a525b68f [machine-unreviewed] ---
100 Tuesday 15
--- seg-b32ff3b007bcffd51080dec3 [machine-unreviewed] ---
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES
--- seg-086862103e2de7a5b3748ccf [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018
--- seg-a1bdb7c5a23fdace551a82a6 [needs-review] ---
There is amortization or extinction of public servant debts, or those considered equivalent, including by a third party. To this end, it is proposed to apply the penalty of imprisonment from four to eight years and a fine that can be increased by half if it is proven that the ownership or possession of goods and values is fraudulently attributed to third parties, the so-called "use of 'oranges'".

In this regard, it is important to highlight that the United Nations Convention against Corruption, internalized by Brazil, "exorts States Parties to criminalize in their legal systems the offense of illicit enrichment, defined as a significant increase in the wealth of a public official through income that cannot be reasonably justified by him/her."

In the administrative sphere, the conduct that leads to the characterization of the illicit enrichment of the public agent is provided for in Law No. 8.429/1992, which "provides for the sanctions applicable to public agents in cases of illicit enrichment in the exercise of a mandate, position, employment or function in the direct, indirect or foundation public administration and establishes other provisions," and we can call it another legislative mechanism to combat corruption, particularly in government institutions that inevitably cause damage to the treasury and society.

The presumed illicit enrichment of the public agent occurs when the public agent manifests signs of administrative improbity, a fact resulting from the flagrantly incompatible patrimonial increase with the corresponding remuneration. This is described in Article 9 of Law No. 8.429/92:

"Article 9. Administrative improbity consisting of illicit enrichment is obtained by obtaining any type of patrimonial advantage improperly due to the exercise of a position, mandate, function, employment or activity in the entities mentioned in Article 1 of this law, and particularly:

...

VII. Acquiring, for oneself or for others, in the exercise of a public mandate, position, employment or function, goods of any nature whose value is disproportionate to the evolution of the agent's patrimony or income;"
--- seg-3c139f316182ac298a47a24a [needs-review] ---
In its turn, disproportionate assets cannot be considered as evidence of illicit enrichment, unless proven otherwise, although they may give rise to a legal presumption. It is inferred that assets disproportionate to income or the normal patrimonial evolution of a public official, acquired during their term of office, represent the acquisition of an undue advantage due to their office (art. 9 caput) and thus constitute an act of improbity. Of course, a civil servant will always have the possibility to prove the legitimacy of their patrimonial increase, such as an inheritance, a prize, or a lawful activity outside of working hours.

The configuration of this type of administrative act of improbity is subject to penalties such as the loss of public office, suspension of political rights, payment of civil fines, prohibition from contracting with the public sector, etc. (art. 12, item I1), all of which are applicable by the judiciary. In turn, it is up to the administration to apply, based on the Statute of Civil Servants of the Union, the penalty of dismissal (art. 132, item IV).

A practical example of this situation would be a civil servant with a salary of R$5,000.00 (five thousand reais), but whose assets include luxury vessels, properties, and vehicles.

Article 12. Independently of criminal, civil, and administrative penalties provided for in specific legislation, the responsible party for an act of improbity is subject to the following sanctions, which may be applied individually or cumulatively according to the gravity of the fact: I - in the case of art. 9, loss of assets or values illegally added to the patrimony, full reimbursement of any damage, loss of public office, suspension of political rights for eight to ten years, payment of a civil fine of up to three times the value of the illicitly acquired assets, and prohibition from contracting with the public sector or receiving fiscal or credit incentives, directly or indirectly, even through a legal entity in which they are a majority shareholder, for a period of ten years;

Unique Paragraph. In determining the penalties provided for in this law, the judge shall consider the extent of the damage caused, as well as the patrimonial benefit obtained by the agent. (I emphasized)

BILL NO. 10,172, OF 2018
(From Mr. Rubens Bueno)
Amends Law No. 1,075, of March 27, 1950, which regulates voluntary blood donation.
DISPOSITION:
ATTACH TO PL-6075/2016.
CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Plenary Consideration
--- seg-393503f153c84547c095ceb7 [needs-review] ---
The National Congress decrees:

Article 1. Law No. 1,075 of March 27, 1950, is hereby amended to include the following article:

"Article 2-A. Voluntary and regular blood donors to Hemocenters or official health institutions are exempt from paying 50% (fifty percent) of the entrance fee to cultural, sporting, and leisure events held throughout the national territory.

§1° O The benefit described in the preceding paragraph shall be granted to those who prove to be regular blood donors, upon presentation of an official document certifying blood donations issued by the respective State or Municipal Health Secretariats.

§ 2. Regular blood donors shall include any person registered with Hemocenters or official health institutions who have, proven to have made at least three donations, in the case of men, and two, in the case of women, within a twelve-month period."

--- seg-19d17bf6693d7537c053e80e [needs-review] ---
JUSTIFICATION
This proposal aims to contribute to the encouragement of voluntary blood donations across the national territory. In Brazil, approximately 3.5 million people undergo blood transfusions. In total, there are 27 coordinating hemocenters and 500 collection services in the country. Currently, only 1.8% of the Brazilian population donates blood. Although the percentage falls within the parameters of the World Health Organization (WHO) - of at least 1% of the population - it is still low in terms of blood stock to meet health needs. Indeed, the Ministry of Health has been working to increase the rate. Blood is

===== PAGE 103 [page-9273d7c26cad5c2ecdccc0fa] =====

Irreplaceable. And those who need it can only obtain it through the generosity of those who donate. This Draft Law aims to reinforce the importance of donation, sensitize new volunteers, and retain donors.

The history of hemotherapy in Brazil over the past three decades has recorded significant advancements in the search for a hemotherapy system that provides the population with a final product that is safe and of quality. This was only possible thanks to the restructuring of services, the legitimization of blood donation as a voluntary, altruistic, and unpaid act, as well as technological advancements, legal frameworks, technical norms, capacitations, and modernization of management. The Brazilian Public Hem Network has been, day by day, fulfilling its mission of ensuring the supply of blood to the entire population in a safe and sustainable manner, seeking the selection of healthy, voluntary, and regular blood donors.

The task of sensitizing blood donors in the Brazilian reality is not an easy or simple one. BILL NO. 10,175, OF 2018
(From Mr. Jerônimo Goergen)
Gives new wording to article 14 of Law 11,947 of June 16, 2009, which provides for the provision of school meals and the Direct Cash Transfer to Schools program to basic education students; amends Laws 10,880 of June 9, 2004, 11,273 of February 6, 2006, 11,507 of July 20, 2007; repeals provisions of Provisional Measure 2,178-36 of August 24, 2001, and Law 8,913 of July 12, 1994; and provides for other measures.

DISPOSITION:
ATTACH PL-4902/2016.

CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Plenary Consideration
The National Congress decrees:

Article 1. Article 14 of Law 11,947 of June 16, 2009, shall be replaced by the following:

"Article 14. At least 30% (thirty percent) of the financial resources transferred by the FNDE, within the scope of the National School Meal Program (PNAE), shall be used for the direct acquisition of food products from family farms and rural family entrepreneurs or their organizations.

(...)".

Article 2. This law shall enter into force on the date of its publication, repealing any contrary provisions.

JUSTIFICATION

The purpose of this legislative proposal is to correct the demonstrated unconstitutionality in the current wording of the legal provision in question, which prioritizes land reform settlements, indigenous traditional communities, and quilombos (a term used to refer to communities of African descendants in Brazil) at the expense of general family farmers who are not part of these communities, in the acquisition of the legal minimum for purchasing products from family farms from the total of financial resources transferred by the FNDE within the scope of the PNAE.

The provision in question is a public policy and support for family farming, which represents 84% of all rural properties in the country and employs at least five million families, according to a 2014 report by the United Nations (UN) entitled "State of Food and Agriculture".

The aforementioned unconstitutionality refers to a blatant violation of the principle of equality, a fundamental norm and symbol of democracy, which indicates fair treatment of citizens.

processes from family farming, at the expense of other family farmers who are not part of these communities.
What is the basis for this disparity, since the difficulties in the field are the same for everyone? Both

BILL NO. 10,176, OF 2018
(From Mr. Celso Russomanno)
Adds to Law No. 8,935, of November 18, 1994, which regulates Article 236 of the Federal Constitution,
providing for notarial and registration services. (Notary Public Law).
DISPOSITION:
TO THE COMMITTEE ON CONSTITUTION, JUSTICE, AND CITIZENSHIP (MERIT AND ART. 54, RICD).
CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Conclusive Consideration by the Committees - Art. 24 II
THE NATIONAL CONGRESS decrees:
Art. 1 - This Law adds a provision to Law No. 8,935, of November 18, 1994, which
regulates Article 236 of the Federal Constitution, providing for notarial and registration services.
Art. 2 - Law No. 8,935, of November 18, 1994, is amended as follows:
Art. 37-A. Natural or legal persons designated by the competent organs of the states and the Federal District, in accordance with state and district legislation, to manage the collection and transfers of resources intended for the compensation of free civil registration acts of natural persons and for the complementation of the minimum revenue of deficitary offices, as well as those responsible for resources intended for the pension funds of registrars and notaries, have the duty to account, as public resource managers, and must document all corresponding acts, as well as submit them to oversight, presenting a detailed documentary report to the respective courts of justice and accounting boards on a semi-annual basis.
§ 1 - The duty to account provided for in the preceding paragraph is independent of any additional regulation in place for its implementation, even if operational rules are established within the competence of the oversight bodies.
Art. 3 - This Law enters into force on the date of its publication.
JUSTIFICATION
Law No. 8.935/94, which provides for notarial and registration services, should also aim to ensure transparency and integrity in the management of public resources. Despite the obligation of any public resource manager to account, since the enactment of the aforementioned norm, as well as subsequent ones on fees, there is a gap to be addressed, either because it would not be justified in the light of public law imperatives, or due to the need to adapt this normative instrument to the current reality and the society's expectations, making this duty clear and unquestionable.
Thus, in compliance with other relevant regulations on the subject and, seeking to fill the aforementioned gap in the best way possible, it was deemed necessary to insert the normative provision in question so that both resources intended for the compensation of registrars related to free acts practiced and the complementation of the minimum revenue of deficitary offices, as well as those intended for the pension fund of registrars and notaries, while public resources, are clearly and formally submitted to oversight.

===== PAGE 107 [page-fa59e9d3113f9386faa99c35] =====

--- seg-b02ea66f948173cfe7af1f02 [machine-unreviewed] ---

To the competent Justice Courts (as already provided for other cases in Article 37 and following of the same Law No. 8.935/94), and to the review of the respective Audit Courts, fulfilling their "end mission" of oversight.

Currently, there is no specific determination regarding the management, allocation, and oversight of these resources, nor is there an obligation to submit them to the competent bodies. In the absence of explicit legal provisions, we have supplied them with this Draft Law.

The Federal Constitution, in particular Article 71, subparagraph II, in conjunction with Article 75, entrusts these Courts with the oversight of "accounting, financial, budgetary, operational, and patrimonial" matters, as well as the judgment of accounts of any individuals responsible for public funds, goods, and values, as in the case at hand.

Indeed, considering that our legislation must be in harmony with the Magna Carta and that, when it comes to public resources, there are no exceptions that allow for any non-compliance with the proposed directives, it becomes imperative to include this legal command, which, in fact, is not innovative but merely aligns with the Major Norm as it should have been this way long ago.

Furthermore, given the current economic and financial situation, with the scarcity of public funds, we have a duty to ensure efficiency in legislative drafting, norming the allocation and correct oversight of available resources. In this way, we will respond to the growing demand of society for efficient and regular management of public resources, minimizing any potential for deviations or arbitrariness regarding this matter.

For the reasons presented, I request the support of my esteemed colleagues for the approval of this important project.

Chamber of Sessions, May 8, 2018.

BILL NO. 10,178, 2018
(From Mr. Celso Russomanno)
Inserts a single paragraph in Article 338 of Law 9,503, of September 23, 1997, which establishes the Brazilian Traffic Code, to require accurate information on fuel volume in the vehicle owner's manual.
DISPOSITION:
ATTACH TO PL-9450/2017.
CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Final Consideration by the Commissions - Article 24, II
The National Congress decrees:
Article 1º O Article 338 of Law 9,503, of September 23, 1997, is amended to include the following single paragraph:
"Article 338. ......................................................................................
Single Paragraph. The owner's manual shall contain accurate information on the maximum volume that the fuel tank can hold, as well as the maximum volume of the reservoir, considering the model and year of the respective vehicle, and informing the acceptable volume variation during refueling." (NR)
Article 2. This law enters into force 180 days after its publication.
JUSTIFICATION
Law 9.503/1997 requires manufacturers, body builders, importers, and manufacturers of motor vehicles to provide, at the time of commercialization, a manual containing traffic rules, infractions, penalties, defensive driving, first aid, and annexes of the Brazilian Traffic Code. This driver's manual is accompanied, in the same volume or in a separate volume, by the owner's manual, with information on each particular vehicle model.
However, it is sometimes difficult, or even impossible, to find information on the fuel volume that the tank can hold. To make matters worse, the volume indicated in the manual may be incorrect. A report published by Sindicombustíveis Resan1 documents the common inconveniences at fuel stations across the country, when drivers question the measured volume at the pump when filling up their tanks, confronting retailers with the car manual and claiming it would be impossible to fuel the volume indicated at the pump.
To assess the situation, the National Federation of Fuel and Lubricant Commerce (Fecombustíveis) commissioned a study that compared the information in the manuals of 13 vehicle models with the actual capacity of their respective tanks2. Only one model had a measured volume identical to that in the manual, while others showed variations of up to 36.5% higher. In other words,

**Justification**

The modernization of consumer relations has driven diversification not only in the way products and services are offered but also in the expansion of payment instruments, particularly in retail trade.

The use of debit and credit cards has moved beyond mere convenience to become a reality in the daily routines of many consumers, who choose this technology for various reasons: security, convenience, speed of transactions, obtaining advantages, expense control, among others.

For individuals with visual impairments, "plastic money" (as credit or debit cards are known) serves as an accessibility tool, as it allows autonomy in payment operations and avoids carrying and constantly handling large amounts of paper currency, which poses security risks.

However, despite the technological dynamism of so-called "terminals" that process payments made with cards, product and service providers have not made available models that effectively meet the needs of this consumer public.

A notice released in 2015 by the National Organization of the Blind in Brazil - ONCB1 criticizes this disparity. It highlights that "the traditional models of machines for credit and debit card payments, which had tactile relief signage for the number 5 and main keys, are rapidly being replaced by debit card machines with touch screens."

It also emphasizes that, "due to their flawed and restrictive design, these machines deprive individuals with visual impairments of the use of touch, subjecting them to significant embarrassment during financial transactions, such as repeatedly trying to enter a PIN until it is blocked, having to pass their card PIN to a known person to enter it, or more seriously, if they are unaccompanied, having to disclose their PIN to a stranger to enter it."

There are also reports that certain establishments force individuals with visual impairments to use their personal mobile phones as payment terminals, or offer optical character recognition (OCR or QR code) technology that, similarly, is not a suitable solution for this consumer public's access to payment information.

Beyond any doubt, these situations are unimaginable in the current stage of accessibility discipline, whose efforts are directed towards promoting and guaranteeing social inclusion and the exercise of rights.

1 http://www.oncb.org.br/node/103. Accessed 03/05/2018.

(From Mr. Felipe Bornier)
Provides for the mandatory inclusion of the customer service telephone number (SAC) on the electronic site of e-commerce stores on the World Wide Web (internet).
DISPACH:
ATTACH TO PL-4189/2012.
CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Plenary Consideration
The National Congress decrees:
Article 1º O Any electronic site of a supplier of products and services, established throughout the national territory, that provides services or sells products through e-commerce on the World Wide Web, must make available to the consumer and include, in a prominent and easily visible location on its main electronic page, the telephone number of the customer service (SAC).
Article 2º O Non-compliance with the provisions of this Law shall subject the infractor to the penalties provided for in Article 56 of Law No. 8,078, of September 11, 1990 - Consumer Defense Code.
Article 3 This law shall enter into force on the date of its official publication.
JUSTIFICATION
This proposal aims to inform the consumer, in an easily accessible location on the electronic site page used in e-commerce, about the customer service (SAC) telephone number.
This relevant information about the SAC telephone number, which relates to the offer, presentation, and advertising, particularly in the context of e-commerce on the internet, although already well established in the discipline of our Consumer Protection and Defense Code (CDC), requires better regulation in federal legislation.
Although there is already regulation on the matter at the sub-legal level, namely Decree No. 7,962, of 2013, which "regulates Law No. 8,078, of September 11, 1990, to provide for contracting in e-commerce", we consider that the norm contained in its Article 21 is not sufficient to curb the frequent abuses committed by various e-commerce sites operating in Brazil.
The fact is that the absence of SAC telephone information persists, and virtual stores, with the following provision:
"Articles The electronic sites or other electronic means used for the offer or conclusion of a consumer contract shall make available, in a prominent and easily visible location, the following information:
I - Business name and supplier's registration number, if any, in the National Register of Natural Persons or in the National Register of Legal Entities of the Ministry of Finance;
II - Physical and electronic address, and other necessary information for its location and contact;” (I have emphasized)

BILL NO. 10,182, OF 2018
(From Mrs. Gorete Pereira)
Amends Law No. 12,318, of August 26, 2010.
DISPACH:
TO THE COMMITTEES ON:
SOCIAL SECURITY AND FAMILY; AND
CONSTITUTION, JUSTICE, AND CITIZENSHIP (MERIT AND ART. 54, RICD).
CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Conclusive Consideration by the Committees - Art. 24 II
The National Congress decrees:
Art. 1. This Law amends Law No. 12,318, of August 26, 2010, to provide for parental alienation and protective measures for children and adolescents in cases of their occurrence.
Art. 2. Articles 2 and 6 of Law No. 12,318, of August 26, 2010, are amended as follows:
“Art. 2. ......................................
Sole Paragraph. ............................................................
VI - to file a false complaint against a parent, relatives of that parent, or grandparents in order to prevent or hinder their coexistence with the child or adolescent;
.......................................” (NR)
“Art. 6. ......................................................................
§ 1. In cases of abusive change of address, impediment or obstruction of family coexistence, the judge may also reverse the obligation to bring or remove the child or adolescent from the parent's residence during the alternation of family coexistence periods.
§ 2. It is the judge's responsibility to avoid the provisional adoption of the measures provided for in clauses II and V to VII of the main provision of this article when there is a minimum indication of the practice of sexual abuse or any crime against one's own child who is a child or adolescent by the parent who has alleged the practice of parental alienation by the other in order to obtain any of the measures referred to in this paragraph.” (NR)
Art. 3. This Law enters into force on the date of its publication.
JUSTIFICATION
In an edition of the well-known Sunday program Fantástico produced by Rede Globo de Televisão that aired on April 8 of this year, a report was broadcast that announced the existence of cases in which a father, allegedly having committed sexual abuse against a minor under eighteen years old,

===== PAGE 116 [page-0d960dca840c9fcd9f0948e2] =====
--- seg-b098ca23fe8cb6474ab712c6 [machine-unreviewed] ---
116 Tuesday 15
--- seg-6627a1d075c033baaae665ec [machine-unreviewed] ---
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES
--- seg-aa8c57033b5af1cdb4636600 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018
--- seg-626a5274906a56cbb22e1379 [needs-review] ---
Over the years, it would come to rely on what the current law on parental alienation (Law No. 12.318 of August 26, 2010) stipulates to actually obtain a change in custody of the child to a shared custody arrangement or its reversal in favor of the father.

In genuine situations, it will be observed, as a result of this behavior and the measures then taken by the judiciary, a complete perversion of the law capable of also enabling the repetition of sexual abuse or crimes against children and adolescents by the parent who has previously committed them, with serious risks of severe harm arising for the physical, sexual and/or psychological integrity and the regular physical and mental development of the victims.

Therefore, it is urgent to adopt legislative measures to improve the current law on parental alienation so that situations like these are avoided.

Following this line of thought, we now propose to amend the provisions of the aforementioned law in order to explicitly state that: a) only the presentation of a false accusation against a parent, their family members, or grandparents to obstruct or hinder their interaction with the child or adolescent (an exemplary form already legally listed) will constitute parental alienation when this fact is properly recognized by the police or judicial authority in an inquiry or proceeding; and b) it is the judge's responsibility to prevent the provisional adoption of protective measures provided for in this legal document, such as changing the custody of the child to a shared arrangement and its reversal, when there is even a slight indication of sexual abuse or any crime against their own minor child (under 18 years old) by the parent who has alleged the practice of parental alienation by the other parent in order to obtain any of these measures.

With these proposed amendments, we believe that the occurrence of situations like those reported in the mentioned television program will be, to some extent, hindered without, however, distorting the current law on parental alienation to remove its desired effectiveness in other cases where this legal document already serves an important function in protecting children and adolescents and their families.

Confident that the importance of this bill and the benefits it may bring from the perspective of protecting children and adolescents will be recognized by my esteemed colleagues, we hope to receive the necessary support for its approval.

Chamber of Sessions, May 9, 2018.

BILL NO. 10,189, 2018
(From Mr. Marcelo Ortiz)
Declares the sweet known as "TAIADA" as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Brazil and the city of Caçapava.

DISPACH:
TO THE COMMITTEES OF:
CULTURE; AND
CONSTITUTION AND JUSTICE AND CITIZENSHIP (ART. 54 RICD).

CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Conclusive Consideration by the Committees - Art. 24 II
The National Congress decrees:

Art. 1. Provides for the recognition of the cultural importance of the sweet known as
“TAIADA”, nationally known and typical of the state of São Paulo, originating from the city of Caçapava, for
the Brazilian tourist circuit.

Art. 2º O The sweet known as “TAIADA” is hereby constituted as Intangible Cultural Heritage
of Brazil for all legal purposes.

Art. 3. This law shall enter into force on the date of its publication.

JUSTIFICATION

"Taiada is a typical sweet from the Brazilian city of Caçapava, in the state of São Paulo, made from
garapa (sugar cane juice), with cassava flour and ginger, resulting in a crumbly texture and enhancing the
spicy flavor.

The production of taiada is artisanal and a family tradition passed down from father to son, mainly
in the rural areas of this municipality. As the sweet is made with ingredients of high nutritional and caloric
value and is easily transportable, it was taken by rural workers to the fields and by soldiers in the army on
marching to be used as an energy source during work and effort, and also to sweeten drinks like coffee with
milk.

The name "taiada" is a corruption of "talhada", the participle of the verb "talhar", which
gently acquired a Caipira accent, becoming popularly known as "taiada".

After the manual cutting of sugar cane, where the best ones are selected, they are transported to
the mill where they are ground. The resulting cassava juice is then poured into a copper pot, boiled for
approximately 90 minutes, until it reaches the desired consistency (a little in cold water and it seems like
candy that can be stretched); taken off the heat and mixed with cassava flour and ground ginger; the mixture
is then poured into a traditional wooden mold in the shape of a square, suitable for this purpose, and left
in the mold for an hour when it hardens, cools and takes its shape, after which it can be removed from the
molds. In the book "Miçangas Folclóricas", by folklorist Francisco Pereira da Silva, known

As Chico Triste, there is a recipe dictated by Benedito Martins.
Those born in Caçapava, or living in the municipality, are affectionately called "taiadas," in reference to the sweet found in that city, with several versions for the origin of this nickname, but almost all are related to young men who served mandatory military service at the Brazilian Army barracks and, upon leaving, would stop at a bar and, among other things, buy the sweet, and those from other cities would bid farewell to the Caçapavenses by calling them "taiada," and despite the sweet no longer being as popular as it once was, the nickname is still widely used.

This justification, extracted from the free encyclopedia, Wikipedia, https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiada, clearly demonstrates the importance of the sweet to our country's popular culture, which is why I present this bill in line with the excellent work of rescuing popular culture formulated by the Municipal Secretary of Culture, Sports, and Leisure of Caçapava, Professor Fabrício Correia, in accordance with the cultural formulations of Mayor Fernando Cid Diniz Borges.

Therefore, we request the support of the Honorable Members of this House for the approval of the present bill.

(From Mrs. Tia Eron)
Amends Article 41-A of Law No. 9,096, of September 19, 1995, to modify the criteria for distributing the resources of the Party Fund, reserving 10% (ten percent) of the Fund's amount for parties that comply with rules regarding the political participation of the Black community.
DISPOSITION:
ATTACH PL-8350/2017.
CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Plenary Consideration
The National Congress decrees:
Article 1. This Law amends Article 41-A of Law No. 9,096, of September 19, 1995, to modify the criteria for distributing the Party Fund, providing for the reservation of 10% (ten percent) of the Fund for equal distribution among parties that comply with legal rules regarding the promotion of the political participation of the Black community.
Article 2º O Article 41-A of Law No. 9,096, of September 19, 1995, is hereby amended to read as follows:
"Article 41-A. Of the total of the Party Fund, to be distributed among parties that meet the constitutional requirements:
I - 5% (five percent) shall be set aside for distribution in equal portions among all parties.
II - 10% (ten percent) shall be set aside for distribution in equal portions to parties that meet the following rules:
a) parties that implement specific programs to promote and ensure the political participation of the Black community;
b) parties that maintain, throughout each legislative year, in the national party organ's direction and at least half of the regional party organs, at least 30% of Black community representatives.
III - 85% (eighty-five percent) shall be distributed among parties in proportion to the votes obtained in the last general election for the Chamber of Deputies.
§ 1. If none of the parties meet the requirements established in subparagraph II, the reserved resources shall be added to the amount established in subparagraph III.
§ 2. For the purposes of subparagraph III, changes in party affiliation shall be disregarded in all cases. (Amended)"
Article 3. This Law shall enter into force on the date of its publication.

**JUSTIFICATION**

It is common knowledge that the recent political reform approved by the National Congress established the Electoral Fund for campaign financing. Despite the creation of this new fund, the rules of the Party Fund remain unchanged. It is worth noting that funds from the Party Fund can also be used for electoral campaigns, although its primary purpose has historically been to cover party expenses. This model has not been significantly altered since the creation of the Fund.

The main objective of this proposal is to modify the distribution and application of Party Fund resources to introduce a system of rewarding parties that meet specific requirements, always aimed at encouraging political participation from "minorized" sectors of our society.

This bill proposes to encourage the participation of the Black community in politics. It is undeniable that there is reluctance in political and party life regarding Black participation, which contrasts with our population's ethnic composition. It is true that Blacks are currently under-represented.

In this context, we believe it is important to change the way resources from the Party Fund are distributed to establish incentive policies for parties aimed at improving our democracy. In other words: a party that meets certain conditions will be rewarded with additional portions of the Party Fund.

As mentioned, our goal is to initiate this new model by establishing requirements related to the political participation of the Black community. Specifically, we propose to reserve 10% (ten percent) of Party Fund resources to be distributed among organizations that:

(a) Implement specific programs to promote and encourage Black community political participation;

(b) Have at least 30% of Black community representatives in the leadership of the national party body and at least half of the regional party bodies.

BILL NO. 10,206, OF 2018
(From Mr. Dr. Sinval Malheiros)
Elevates the Egg Festival of Bastos/SP to the status of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Brazil.

DISPOSITION:
TO THE COMMITTEES OF:
CULTURE; AND
CONSTITUTION AND JUSTICE AND CITIZENSHIP (ART. 54 RICD).
CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Conclusive Consideration by the Committees - Art. 24 II
THE NATIONAL CONGRESS decrees:

Art. 1. This Law aims to recognize the importance of the Egg Festival of Bastos/SP as the main event promoting the significance and trade of eggs in Brazil.

Art. 2. The Egg Festival of Bastos/SP is established as intangible cultural heritage of Brazil, for all legal purposes.

Art. 3. This Law enters into force on the date of its publication.

JUSTIFICATION
Bastos is a Brazilian municipality, located in the interior of the state of São Paulo, with a population of approximately twenty thousand inhabitants. It is known, especially, for its egg production, being known as “the national capital of eggs”. And as one of the reasons that underpin its importance in domestic egg production, there is the Egg Festival of Bastos.

The city, founded by Japanese immigrants, began to invest in egg production after World War II as a way to revive the local economy. Thanks to tireless and excellent work, the activity strengthened and the city consolidated as a reference pole in the area, with more than seven decades dedicated to the practice, considered the main exponent of the segment since the 1960s.

The municipality has over 33 million birds intended for egg production, and according to the local Rural Syndicate president in 2017, Mr. Katsuhide Maki, the farms of the municipality produce 216 units per second, with 18.7 million eggs per day. Annually, Bastos produces around 10 billion eggs, which represents approximately 25% of Brazil's annual production of 40 billion.

Bastos, therefore, producing alone 25% of a food of immense nutritional value and fundamental importance to the Brazilian, being a rich protein and vitamin source at a price generally more accessible than red meat, for example.

Given such a redemption brought about by egg production, Bastos began to hold its Egg Festival. The event was born in 1948 and gained importance over time. Before

===== PAGE 125 [page-c18fe739c47e6dca6b7a8a4b] =====
--- seg-9b271b47f3ef34e6456118d6 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018
--- seg-1496e32e4c71d0206cf2144f [machine-unreviewed] ---
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES
--- seg-6fa9ca90b2d0b43379e436c1 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Tuesday 15 125
--- seg-068044946fcaf8c549c44789 [needs-review] ---
Held every five years, the festival has become annual and today approaches its 59th edition, highlighting the
importance of the location and its dedication to egg production.
It is an event of extreme importance and attractiveness for the surrounding regions, attracting the
interest of numerous producers in the sector. In 2017, for example, eighty-two companies were exhibitors at
the event, demonstrating its magnitude and its growing importance. From 2016 to 2017, there was a 30%
increase in the number of exhibitors.
The event offers a little bit of everything: recreational activities related to eggs (contests to see who eats
the most), competitions aimed at assessing the quality of eggs and concluding with the best one, workshops
and lectures intended to disseminate information about the food, its production and techniques, and even
serving as a pole for technological discussions on the topic.
Undeniably, the festival functions as a true driving force for egg production in Brazil, with characteristics
of cultural, informational, educational, and commercial diffusion, demonstrating that it is a cultural and
intangible heritage. The tradition and quality of what is produced there are of fundamental importance not
only for Bastos, or even for the large state of São Paulo, but for Brazil, as it is the largest exponent of
production of one of the main national foods.
For all these reasons, we believe that the Egg Festival of Bastos/SP requires formal recognition by this
National Congress and, subsequently, by the Executive Power, by sanctioning its existence as a cultural and
intangible heritage of our nation.
Brazil needs to learn to value its significant traditions more, which transmit good customs, and perfect
them, something that Bastos has been an example of. This is because it has transformed this recreational
event into a commercial opportunity and a means of disseminating knowledge and technologies, without
losing the joy and leisure provided by the festival.
Thus, we submit this proposal to the consideration of the esteemed colleagues and urge them to approve
it. Because taking care of cities (and their traditions) is taking care of people.
Chamber of Sessions, May 9, 2018.
DR. SINVAL MALHEIROS
Doctor and Federal Deputy (PODEMOS/SP)

**LEGISLATIVE DECREE PROJECT No. 923, 2018**
(From Mr. Jerônimo Goergen)
Suspends the effects of MP Instruction Normative No. 2, of January 24, 2018, which establishes rules and guidelines for the execution of a service contract to be concluded between the Union and federal official financial institutions, to act as the Union's mandataries in the operational management of transfer contracts, in accordance with Decree 6,170 of July 25, 2007, as well as all acts derived from the aforementioned normative instruction.

**DISPOSITION:**
Attach to PDC-905/2018.

**CONSIDERATION:**
Proposal Subject to Plenary Consideration
The National Congress decrees:

**Article 1:** The effects of MP Instruction Normative No. 2, of January 24, 2018, which establishes rules and guidelines for the execution of a service contract to be concluded between the Union and federal official financial institutions, to act as the Union's mandataries in the operational management of transfer contracts, in accordance with Decree 6,170 of July 25, 2007, as well as all acts derived from the aforementioned normative instruction, are hereby suspended.

**Article 2:** This legislative decree enters into force on the date of its official publication.

**JUSTIFICATION**
We received with undeniable opposition the news that the Ministry of Planning, in response to complaints from the Federal Economic Bank, issued Instruction Normative 2/18, a new legal framework for the execution of service contracts to be concluded between the Union and federal official financial institutions, as the Union's mandataries in the operational management of transfer contracts.

The government's decision to increase the administration fees charged by agreements signed with ministries and financed with parliamentary appropriation resources was taken unilaterally and without any prior dialogue with this House, members of Congress, and directly affected municipalities.

The administration fees traditionally charged at levels of 2.5% on the value of each individual appropriation, practiced in recent years, have been catapulted to percentages that can reach around 12% of the total value to be transferred. Highly questionable in terms of legality, morality, and constitutionality, the measure harms the execution of vital works and services for the country's needy population, already so neglected by federal public policies.

Therefore, as it is the National Congress's competence, according to Article 49, paragraph V, of the Federal Constitution, "to suspend executive acts that exceed the regulatory power or the limits of legislative delegation", I present this legislative decree project to suspend the effects of MP Instruction Normative No. 2, of January 24, 2018, and I count on the support of my fellow members of Congress in the approval of this matter.

Chamber of Sessions, May 2, 2018.

Deputado JERÔNIMO GOERGEN

LEGISLATIVE DECREE PROJECT No. 924, of 2018
(From Mr. Paulo Pimenta and others)
Suspends Decree No. 9,355, of April 25, 2018.
DISPOSITION:
TO THE COMMITTEES OF:
MINES AND ENERGY AND
CONSTITUTION, JUSTICE, AND CITIZENSHIP (MERIT AND ART. 54, RICD)
CONSIDERATION:
Proposition Subject to Plenary Consideration
The National Congress decrees:
Art. 1. Decree No. 9,355, of April 25, 2018, is hereby suspended.
Art. 2. This legislative decree shall enter into force on the date of its publication.
--- seg-cea2b507ebcab555e09c0f75 [needs-review] ---
**Justification**

The participation of state-owned companies in economic activity should be guided by significant collective interest or national security imperatives, in order to achieve goals such as ensuring national development and reducing social and regional inequalities, among others, as established by our Federal Constitution.

Indirect public administration, which includes state-owned companies, must adhere to constitutional principles of legality, impersonality, morality, publicity, and efficiency. The general need to bid is essential in this regard, even for public companies and mixed economy societies.

According to Article 173, §1, of the Federal Constitution, the law will establish the legal statute for public companies, mixed economy societies, and their subsidiaries that engage in economic activity related to the production or commercialization of goods or the provision of services, including provisions on bidding and contracting for works, services, purchases, and alienations.

Law No. 13.303 of June 30, 2016, known as the Legal Statute of State-Owned Companies, regulated Article 173, §1, and established the legal statute for public companies, mixed economy societies, and their subsidiaries within the scope of the Union, states, Federal District, and municipalities.

===== PAGE 129 [page-e05b2f84e68686364ff7bc92] =====
--- seg-ad73a0e0bbc6b04cc62cd1d0 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018
--- seg-5bbe59d88f0e1603fb434f63 [machine-unreviewed] ---
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES
--- seg-3e13f1e284aedae32d647268 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Tuesday 15 129
--- seg-4997785bfce5ea501cb64051 [needs-review] ---
Section 5 of Article 1 of Law No. 13.303/2016 is clear in defining that for the public company and the mixed economy society that participate in a consortium in the condition of operator are subject to the bidding rules provided in the Legal Statute of State-Owned Enterprises, as it reads:
--- seg-c067766974fa84f3b8feb4ce [machine-unreviewed] ---
§ 5. Public companies and mixed economy societies that participate in a consortium, as provided in Article 279 of Law No. 6,404 of December 15, 1976, shall be subject to the regime established in this Law, in the condition of operator.
--- seg-da00df8929fa91d80e43a018 [machine-unreviewed] ---
In accordance with Article 28 of Law No. 13.303/2016, contracts with third parties for the provision of services to public companies and mixed economy societies, including engineering and advertising, the acquisition and rental of goods, and the alienation of goods and assets forming part of their respective patrimony, must be preceded by a tender process.

Therefore, the procurement of goods and services by consortia operated by Petrobras and the assignment by the state-owned company of rights for the exploration, development, and production of oil and natural gas should be preceded by a tender process, and the bidding process must comply with the requirements established by Law No. 13.303/2016.

Article 1 of Decree No. 9.355 of April 25, 2018, establishes a special procedure for the assignment of rights for the exploration, development, and production of oil and natural gas by Petrobras, as provided for in Article 29, Article 61, paragraph (1), and Article 63 of Law No. 9.478 of August 6, 1997, and in Article 31 of Law No. 12.351 of December 22, 2010.

It is important to note that: Article 29 of Law No. 9.478/1997 only allows for the transfer of the concession contract; Article 61, paragraph (1), essentially aims to prevent favoritism to Petrobras in the acquisition of rights related to petroleum activities; and Article 63 only authorizes Petrobras to form consortia. Article 31 of Law No. 12.351/2010 is generic and applicable to all companies, except for the sole paragraph, which does not allow Petrobras to assign rights related to its minimum participation.

Furthermore, all these legal provisions predate the promulgation of Law No. 13.302/2016.

Thus, Decree No. 9.355/2018 exceeds regulatory power and the limits of legislative delegation by establishing a special procedure for the assignment of rights for the exploration, development, and production of oil, natural gas, and other fluid hydrocarbons by Petrobras.

It is worth noting that the Legal Framework of State-Owned Companies was not even mentioned in Decree No. 9.355/2018, in an attempt to evade current legislation, which the normative act of the Executive Branch clearly violates.

"Strictly across the country, public transportation fares undergo adjustments based, typically, on inflation indices. Therefore, CBTU claims mere inflation loss compensation.

However, in the specific case of Recife, to give an example, the fare correction will be significantly higher than the accumulated inflation during the period since the last adjustment. This adjustment occurred in February 2012, when the fare was set at R$ 1.60. With monetary updating based on IGP-M (FGV), this value would today be R$ 2.27, well below the proposed R$ 3.00 increase. CBTU adjusted the fare by an incredible 24.3% above mere monetary correction.

In addition to the inconsistency of the justification that claims monetary correction while there was an adjustment above accumulated inflation, the increase is abusive and sudden, generating a high degree of uncertainty and economic-financial instability for public service users.

Access to public transportation is a social right guaranteed in the Federal Constitution (Article 6). The purpose of this proposal is to protect the fundamental rights of the population, preventing setbacks in sensitive issues regarding the basic rights of the Brazilian citizen.

Article 49, Clause V, of the Federal Constitution (CF) attributes an extremely important exclusive competence to the National Congress, namely, the power to invalidate executive normative acts that exceed the regulatory power. Furthermore, Clauses X and XI confer to this body the competences of "inspecting and controlling, directly or through any of its chambers, the acts of the executive power, including those of indirect administration" and of "ensuring the preservation of its legislative competence in the face of the normative attribution of the other powers."

Therefore, it can be observed that the aforementioned increase, authorized through the CBTU Board of Directors (CONAD), far exceeded the regulatory power granted to the executive power, being absolutely incompatible with the guiding principles of the 1988 Federal Constitution.

Thus, considering that this fare increase represents a clear disrespect for the constitutional order - characterizing, therefore, a flagrant "excession of regulatory power or of the limits of legislative delegation," as per Article 49, Clause V of the Magna Carta - it is incumbent upon the National Congress, hearing the just concerns of the population, to, through this legislative decree, guarantee access to public transportation by invalidating Item 09 of the minutes of the 364th (three hundred sixty-fourth) Regular Meeting of the Board of Directors of the Brazilian Company of Urban Trains - CBTU, held on February 26, 2018, which approves the fare increase for metro in various Brazilian capitals.

Chamber of Sessions, May 10, 2018."

PROJECT OF RESOLUTION
N.º 312, OF 2018
(From Mr. Eduardo Cury)
Amends the Internal Rules of the Chamber of Deputies, approved by Resolution n.º 17, of September 21, 1989, to provide for requests subject to deliberation by the Plenary.
DISPOSITION:
ATTACH TO PRC-60/2015.
CONSIDERATION:
Proposition Subject to Plenary Consideration
The Chamber of Deputies decides:
Article 1. This Resolution amends Article 117 of the Internal Rules of the Chamber of Deputies, approved by Resolution n.º 17, of September 21, 1989, as follows:
“Article 117........................................................................................
§ 2º O The author or first signatory of any request provided for in this article must be present in the Plenary to direct the vote, under penalty of its automatic rejection by the President.
§ 3º (§2º Renumerated).
§ 4º (§3º Renumerated).
§ 5º (§4º Renumerated).” (Amended).
Article 2. This Resolution shall enter into force on the date of its publication.
JUSTIFICATION
It is frequent during regular and extraordinary sessions of this House that members present requests as a legitimate form of obstruction to the progress of sessions, or as a means to ensure the postponement of votes on certain matters.
Despite the total legitimacy of using requests as a form of obstruction, it is recurrent throughout sessions the reading, direction, and voting of these requests without the presence of the author. This is because, although they present a request, often the author or first signatory is not present in the Plenary to direct the vote.
For this reason, as a means of ensuring that the authors of these requests are present in the Plenary – to exercise their legitimate role of directing the votes on their requests – I submit this resolution project to the consideration of this House and request the support of the other members for its approval.
Chamber of Sessions, April 26, 2018.
Depute Eduardo Cury

## RESOLUTION DRAFT

**NO. 314, 2018**
**(From Mr. Rodrigo Garcia and others)**

Designates a space in the Chamber of Deputies as "Deputado Joaquim Nabuco" and provides for other measures.

**DISPOSAL:**

To the Presidency of the Chamber of Deputies

**CONSIDERATION:**

Proposition subject to plenary consideration

The Chamber of Deputies Presidency resolves:

**Article 1:** The space in the Chamber of Deputies' Noble Hall shall be designated "Deputado Joaquim Nabuco" and will house a bronze bust of the personality and a corresponding plaque.

**Article 2:** The House's technical bodies, after study, shall indicate an appropriate location within the Noble Hall for the designation of the space and the placement of the bust.

**Article 3:** The Chamber of Deputies Presidency shall arrange for the fabrication of a plaque with the appropriate inscriptions for the tribute and shall set a date for its unveiling.

**Article 4:** This Resolution shall enter into force on the date of its publication.

**JUSTIFICATION**

This draft aims to honor the extraordinary figure of Joaquim Nabuco (J. Aurélio Barreto N. de Araújo), known and admired as an intellectual, writer, sociologist, jurist, diplomat, and, most importantly, as one of the icons of the abolitionist movement in Brazil, by placing his bust in a suitable location.

Joaquim Nabuco was born in Recife on August 19, 1849, the son of Senator Nabuco de Araújo and his wife Ana Benigna de Sá Barreto. He passed away in Washington, USA, on January 17, 1910.

He grew up within influential families of Pernambuco's politics. His father, "the Nabuco de Araújo" family - father and grandfather - were senators of the Empire; his mother's side was "the Paes Barreto" family.

He entered the diplomatic service and served in London and Washington from 1876 to 1879. He was later drawn to politics, captivated by the abolitionist cause, which he dedicated himself to throughout his life.

From 1879 to 1889, he served as a Federal Deputy for the state of Pernambuco, elected by the Liberal Party, where he stood out as the main parliamentary leader in the abolitionist struggle.

Ahead of his time, Joaquim Nabuco not only advocated for the end of slavery; he also fought for the basic rights of newly freed slaves, such as education and fair employment. He also fiercely advocated for land reform and the establishment of a secular state.

Upon the proclamation of the Republic in 1889, he staunchly defended the monarchy and withdrew from public life to dedicate himself to study and his literary works.

During this period, he practiced law and journalism; he cultivated relationships with prominent figures of Brazilian literature, such as Machado de Assis, José Veríssimo, and Lúcio de Mendonça. It is believed that the creation of the Brazilian Academy of Letters in 1897 was due to the gatherings of these privileged minds.

RESOLUTION DRAFT
No. 315, 2018
(By Mrs. Iracema Portella)
Draft Resolution establishing the Maria da Penha Medal within the Chamber of Deputies.
--- seg-b23e50038b17ea21b31d34a5 [needs-review] ---
**DISPENSE:**
**TO THE BOARD OF DEPUTIES AND
TO THE COMMITTEE ON CONSTITUTION, LAW AND CITIZENSHIP (ART. 54 RICD)**
**CONSIDERATION:**
Proposal Subject to Plenary Consideration
The Chamber of Deputies resolves:
**Art. 1** The Maria da Penha Medal is hereby established, to be awarded by the Chamber of Deputies to individuals, institutions, and social movements, both national and foreign, who have distinguished themselves through significant initiatives in the fight against violence against women.
**Unique Paragraph** The Maria da Penha Medal may be awarded posthumously, subject to the conditions set forth in this Resolution.
**Art. 2** The Maria da Penha Medal shall be awarded by the Chamber of Deputies' Women's Secretariat and the President of the Chamber of Deputies.
**§1** The Maria da Penha Medal shall consist of a minted medal featuring the effigy of Maria da Penha, a domestic violence victim who inspired the creation of Law No. 11.340 of August 7, 2006.
**§2** The Maria da Penha Medal shall be awarded annually at a solemn session, preferably on September 22.
**Art. 3** Proposals for the award of the Maria da Penha Medal may be submitted in writing to the Chamber of Deputies' Women's Secretariat by any Federal Deputy.
**§1** Proposals should include a biography or brief history of the suggested candidate, with explicit reference to significant initiatives in the fight against violence against women that would justify the award of the Maria da Penha Medal.
**§2** Proposals should adhere to the parameters and deadlines announced by the Chamber of Deputies' Women's Secretariat.
**Art. 4** The selection of the award recipients shall be made by a majority of the Members of the Parliamentary Group.

**Female Chamber of Deputies**

**Article 5** The Chamber of Deputies' Desk shall issue the necessary instructions for the conferment of the Maria da Penha Medal within thirty days of the publication of this Resolution.

**Article 6** This Resolution shall enter into force on the date of its publication.

**Justification**

The proposal for the Maria da Penha Medal, to be conferred by the Chamber of Deputies, aims to honor individuals, institutions, and social movements, both national and international, that, with the same spirit of struggle as Maria da Penha, have distinguished themselves through significant initiatives in the fight against violence against women.

Above all, it is a recognition of the historical role played by the Brazilian woman Maria da Penha in the struggle for women's rights. In 1983, Maria da Penha was victimized by her then-husband with a gunshot wound to the back while she was sleeping, and as a result of this assault, she became paraplegic. After other violences by her ex-husband, Maria da Penha initiated a long and exhausting legal process that took 19 years and 6 months until her ex-husband's conviction in 2002 to eight years in prison.

More than the conviction of her aggressor, Maria da Penha's struggle led the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights of the Organization of American States (OAS) to condemn Brazil in 2001 for negligence, omission, and tolerance regarding domestic violence against women, and to recommend the adoption of public policies aimed at preventing, punishing, and eradicating violence against women. As a direct consequence of this condemnation, the National Congress made new efforts to approve legislation aimed at preventing and punishing domestic violence in Brazil.

After years of debates, the National Congress enacted and the President of the Republic sanctioned Law 11.340 of August 7, 2006, deservedly known as the "Maria da Penha Law," which establishes mechanisms to curb domestic and family violence against women, in accordance with Article 226, § 8 of the Federal Constitution, the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, and the Inter-American Convention to Prevent, Punish and Eradicate Violence against Women; provides for the creation of Domestic and Family Violence against Women Courts; amends the Criminal Procedure Code, the Penal Code, and the Penal Execution Code; and establishes other provisions.

Despite the landmark represented by the Maria da Penha Law, the sad reality is that the story of domestic violence suffered by Maria da Penha still repeats itself daily in thousands of Brazilian homes. Some data from the Maria da Penha Institute highlight this dramatic scenario: (i) every 2 seconds a woman is a victim of physical or verbal violence in Brazil; (ii) every 2.6 seconds a woman is a victim of verbal abuse; (iii) every 6.3 seconds a woman is a victim of a threat of violence; (iv) every 2 minutes a woman is a victim of a firearm; (v) every 22.5 seconds a woman is a victim of

INDICATION No. 5.181, 2018
(From Mr. Weliton Prado)
Recommends to the Ministry of Cities urgent measures to suspend the abusive 88.8% increase in the fare charged to users of the BH/Contagem Metro.

DISPOSITION:
PUBLISH. FORWARD.

Most esteemed Minister:
Minas Gerais is once again indignant at the absurd news that the fare charged to users of the BH/Contagem Metro will increase by 88.8% starting next Friday, May 11, 2018, rising from R$ 1.80 to R$ 3.40.

Now, what public discussions were held with transport users to determine fares? What cost breakdown was made public for the population to justify such an increase? And as for the deadline for defining the increase and the start of new fare implementation?

Inflation in 2017 was 2.95% and they want to impose an 88.8% fare increase on users? With this increase, what benefits and investments will be made in service provision for consumers who use the BH/Contagem Metro? What investments have been made in recent years?

The current value, according to a publication in the newspaper O Tempo, in this Tuesday, May 8, 2018 edition, will be the highest practiced among the five capitals where the Brazilian Urban Trains Company (CBTU) operates. And absurdly, the BH/Contagem Metro is only 28 km long. In Recife, for example, where the fare - even with the announced increase - will be lower than in Belo Horizonte, the metro has three lines and covers a total of 71 km, passing through 4 municipalities.

Comparing all the regions managed by CBTU, Belo Horizonte is the one that raises the most money in the country, however, the population does not see a return on what they pay. Absurdly, in addition to maintaining services from other states, since what is collected by the Belo Horizonte Metro goes to the company's single cash box, Minas Gerais is not treated as a priority when it comes to line expansion and improvements, a saga that has been dragging on for decades, marked by a game of "pass the buck", neglect and total apathy.

And to make matters worse, CBTU, once again, wants to shift the blame for poor management onto the "shoulders" of Minas Gerais users. The company shows no sensitivity, coherence, or efficiency. It seems unaware of the poor quality of services offered to the population, the bad working conditions imposed on metro employees, the current economic crisis in the country, the high number of unemployed, and the population's budget difficulties. The decision taken was disrespectful and, without a doubt, abusive and completely contrary to the current moment when the population demands transparency, efficient use of public resources collected, fair fares, and quality service.

In light of the above, it is necessary that the Ministry of Cities immediately suspend the 88.8% fare increase that will be charged to users of the BH/Contagem Metro and conduct a transparent and public process on the real need for fare composition and the investments that will be made in the population's benefit.

Chamber of Sessions, May 8, 2018.

WELITON PRADO
Federal Deputy - PROS/MG
Consumer Defense Commission

1. Manoel Martins de Oliveira;
2. Marlon dos Reis Lopes;
3. Francisco Inocêncio de Moura; and
4. Alvin Correa Faria Municipal Center for Child Education

These schools did not receive a sufficient number of textbooks to meet the needs of all enrolled students. There are classrooms where more than 40% of the students do not have a textbook, therefore lacking the minimum conditions for learning. Our children arrive at school and unfortunately do not have a minimum material for study. This is absurd! At the time of doing an exercise, each student wants to have their own book. Each one has their own pace and difficulties. Many cannot finish exercises in class and, to make matters worse, they cannot take the book home because the books need to be shared with students of the other shift. This puts the students' learning at risk.

There is a shortage of textbooks for all subjects to meet the needs of all enrolled students, in addition to a shortage of books for teachers.

- As per the FNDE website, "The FNDE distributes textbooks according to projections from the school census two years prior to the program year, which is the census available at the time of school selection processing."

- This distribution criterion, which generates a book shortage due to a technical deficiency in program management, has severe consequences for the students' learning in the region.

- The FNDE proposes to manage these fluctuations through redistribution, from schools with excess books to those with book shortages, or by using the technical reserve (a percentage of books made available to state education secretariats to accommodate new classes and enrollments).

INDICATION No. 5.185, 2018
(From Mr. Renzo Braz)
Recommends to the Minister of State that the necessary measures be adopted to regulate and make it viable
for the Federal Savings Bank to finance the entirety of the property related to housing, as well as reduce the
corresponding interest rates.
DISPOSITION:
PUBLISH. FORWARD.
Honorable Minister,
While we congratulate you on the efforts made so far in the framework of housing financing programs, we
emphasize the need for more effective measures to make it viable for the Federal Savings Bank (CEF) to
finance 100% of the property related to housing, as well as reduce the corresponding interest rates.
We thus aim to ensure that housing is a right accessible to all citizens, particularly the less favored
segment, who, in most cases, do not have any capital to provide as an "entry" or to cover residual values.
In fact, various media outlets repeatedly report that CEF has been applying financing interest rates above
those practiced by other financial institutions, including private ones.
It is important to highlight the report published on the UOL's economic website on March 27, 2018, with
the title: "Caixa loses leadership in housing financing for the fourth consecutive month."
According to the aforementioned article, until October 2017, CEF had always been the leader in housing
financing, far ahead of the second place in both the number of financed properties and values. In November,
it dropped to fourth place, behind Itaú Unibanco, Santander, and Bradesco, a situation that persisted in
December. In January 2018, Bradesco was first, followed by Santander, Caixa, and Itaú.
The fact is that, as published on the financial institution's own website, "since its creation in 1861, Caixa
has always sought to be more than just a bank, but a truly present institution in the lives of millions of
Brazilians. (...) It also appears at the moment of helping the population, through government social
programs, such as Bolsa Família - which benefits over 13 million Brazilians, FIES, and Minha Casa, Minha
Vida Program. (...) Throughout its history, Caixa has established close relations with the population by
meeting their immediate needs, such as savings, loans, FGTS, Social Integration Program (PIS),
Unemployment Insurance, educational credit, housing financing, and social benefit transfers."1

real estate market and the Construction Civil sector.

**INDICATION No. 5.187, 2018**
**(From Mr. Weliton Prado)**
Suggests to the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock and Supply (MAPA), through the Minas Gerais Supply Centers S.A (Ceasa/MG), urgent measures to restore the trading hours of small producers and family farmers' products, currently held on Fridays at the Uberlândia unit in the Triangulo Mineiro region in the afternoon.

**DISPACH:**
**PUBLISH. FORWARD.**

Excellency,

Small producers and family farmers were surprised by another arbitrary and undiscussed decision by the Uberlândia Ceasa, which now aims to change the trading hours of products held at the unit on Fridays.

The trading has always been held in the afternoon to allow producers from Uberlândia and the entire region the necessary time to travel and organize their products. Indeed, most of them harvest their food in the morning to bring to Ceasa in the afternoon and offer fresh, new, and quality food/products to consumers over the weekend, as reinforced to our office by Zezinho Mendonça.

The change to morning hours should only occur after extensive discussion and consensus. The change drastically affects the lives of many people, the quality of products, not to mention the economic impact of the measure, which could lead to reduced purchases by the population and the safety of everyone with early morning displacements.

It is unbelievable that Ceasa, instead of focusing on solving problems at the unit, simply decides to change the trading hours of products without extensive discussion, without justification, and without consensus.

I am the author of the Chamber of Deputies Project of Law No. 59/2015, which establishes the National Plan for the Supply of Horticultural, Fruit, and Flower Products – PLANHORT – currently under review in the Senate after being approved by the Chamber of Deputies.

Therefore, we know and fight for the improvements and valorization of producers who trade at Ceasa. The suffering is immense and repeats every year.

According to UN data, family farming produces approximately 80% of the food consumed and preserves 75% of the planet's agricultural resources. In Brazil, family farmers are responsible for most of the food that reaches the population's table, ensuring food security, rural family permanence, and environmental preservation. There is no way to accept such disrespect, and the consequences of this measure will be negative for the budgets of families who depend on the Uberlândia Ceasa to trade their products; for consumers who may see product quality decrease; and for the economy of Uberlândia and the region.

Chamber Sessions Room, May 8, 2018.
--- seg-32b9577adf007c93542bae72 [machine-unreviewed] ---
WELITON PRADO
FEDERAL DEPUTY – PROS/MG

--- seg-909ea99cdd7dd6a1b7e1c649 [needs-review] ---
MEMORANDUM:
FOR PUBLICATION. FOR FORWARDING.

TO: Honorable Minister of National Integration

Unfortunately, in my opinion, the Federal Government took a precipitate decision in
suspending the Water Truck Operation in 18 municipalities of Paraiba after cutting two-thirds of the resources
for water distribution, especially in rural areas, believing that significant rainfall had occurred in the cities.

However, not all municipalities have experienced significant reservoir replenishment, which could further
harm those living with water scarcity. There are regions that did not receive sufficient rainfall to even
increase reservoir levels by 10%. In these areas, the drought continues, and there is no water supply in the
city other than the water trucks.

Despite recent rainfall, municipalities continue to face difficulties in water distribution. The Federal
Government's measure was extreme. A survey should have been conducted beforehand to identify cities
with no rainfall and then reduce the amount, but cancelling it entirely at once became very complicated for
some cities, penalizing them.

Approximately 70,000 people, mostly from rural areas, who were being supplied through the water
trucks operation, are still facing difficulties in accessing potable water. Therefore, we request that the
operation be resumed immediately to avoid further disruptions to the beneficiaries.

Given the undeniable social impact of the issue, we count on your recognized sensitivity in approving
this Indication, with the resumption of water supply through water trucks in the rural areas of the
Paraiba municipalities of Assunção, Barra de Santana, Boqueirão, Campina Grande, Caturité, Coxixola,
Fagundes, Gurjão, Lagoa Seca, Livramento, Queimadas, Parari, Santa Luzia, Santo André, São José do
Sabugi, São José dos Cordeiros, Serra Branca, and Taperoá, which we suggest to Your Excellency as an
important and urgent measure.

Chamber of Sessions, May 9, 2018.

Rômulo Gouveia
Federal Deputy
PSD-PB

**INDICATION No. 5.189, 2018**
(From Mr. Rômulo Gouveia)
Suggests to the Most Excellent Health Minister that the Mobile Component of Oral Health Care - Mobile Dental Unit (UOM) be implemented in the municipality of São Domingos do Cariri, state of Paraíba.

**DISPACH**
PUBLISH. FORWARD.

Most Excellent Health Minister:

The results of the latest oral health conditions survey of the Brazilian population (SB Brasil 2003) revealed an extremely alarming situation. According to data published on the Ministry of Health's website1, at that time, there were over 30 million edentulous people in the country, while almost the entire adult population had dental caries.

Since then, the topic has become an increasingly priority in the primary health care component offered by the Unified Health System (SUS). Among the various actions of the National Oral Health Policy, the Mobile Component of Oral Health Care, with the installation of Mobile Dental Units (UOM), is an extremely effective action for the care of our population. It specifically caters to those segments with difficulties in accessing health units.

The state of Paraíba has 223 municipalities, many of which have extensive rural areas. In this context, we consider that extending such assistance to all municipalities of the state will bring significant benefits to our population.

In light of the above, Mr. Minister, we suggest that the Mobile Component of Oral Health Care - Mobile Dental Unit (UOM) be installed in the municipality of São Domingos do Cariri/PB, which is fully justified under the proposed terms, as it is important and urgent.

Chamber of Sessions, May 9, 2018.

Deputado RÔMULO GOUVEIA
PSD-PB
