**PROPOSAL FOR INSPECTION AND CONTROL No. 168, 2018**
(By Mr. Patrus Ananias and Mr. João Daniel)
Proposes that the Commission of Financial Inspection and Control, with the assistance of the Union Accounts Court (TCU), carry out an inspection and control act regarding the contract for the provision of business communication consulting services between Centrais Elétricas Brasileiras S.A. (Eletrobras) and RP Brasil Comunicações Ltda (FSB Comunicação).

**DISPACH**
**TO THE COMMISSION OF FINANCIAL INSPECTION AND CONTROL**

**CONSIDERATION**
Proposition subject to internal review within the Commissions

Mr. President,

Based on Article 100, § 1, in conjunction with Article 24, X, Article 60, II, and Article 61, § 1, of the Internal Regulation of the Chamber of Deputies, and Articles 71, IV and VII of the Federal Constitution, and after consultation with the Plenary of this Commission, I propose, with the assistance of the Union Accounts Court (TCU), to carry out an inspection and control act regarding the contract for the provision of business communication consulting services between Centrais Elétricas Brasileiras S.A. (Eletrobras) and RP Brasil Comunicações Ltda (FSB Comunicação).

**JUSTIFICATION**

On April 24, 2018, the website Sportlight published that Centrais Elétricas Brasileiras S.A. (Eletrobras) contracted RP Brasil Comunicações Ltda to conduct a campaign against the very company it was contracted by. Given the seriousness of the allegation, the approval of the Proposal for Inspection and Control is of extreme importance to examine the validity of this contract. We reproduce the text published on Sportlight:

"Eletrobrás paid nearly R$ 2 million to worsen its own image"

Column notes, television comments, and agendas constructed to demonstrate the urgent need for privatization were driven by the FSB Comunicação group, through a "half-price" bidding process.

By Lúcio de Castro, Sportlight, published April 24, 2018 - 14h25

Wilson Ferreira Júnior assumed the Eletrobrás with a specific mission given by Michel Temer: to conduct the privatization process.

Officially referred to as "deregulation" or "democratization of capital," the privatization of the company, a priority of the Michel Temer government, received a significant boost on September 20, 2017, when the state signed a contract with RP Brasil Comunicações, part of the FSB Comunicação group, the country's largest press office.

**CONTRACT OBJECT**

The contract ECE-DJS 1252/2017, obtained by the reporting team through the Access to Information Law (LAI): "to advise Eletrobras on communication related to the majority shareholder's privatization project for the company."

In search of public mobilization and a favorable environment for privatization, the company adopted as a strategy the dissemination of a scenario of miseries and problems of the state-owned company. To do this, it was necessary to engage so-called opinion formers, the press, release notes in newspaper columns, arm economic commentators, and set the media agenda, always presenting a scenario that made such privatization urgent, accelerated by the federal government's haste to finalize the deal. The company denies such bias and states that the contract emphasizes the need to "preserve the company's positive image," although it admits that the disclosure "does not omit negative data such as financial losses or gross debt exceeding R$ 45 billion" (see "the other side at the end of the report").

According to the plan outlined in the contract, a "scenario analysis" was conducted, followed by the so-called "mapping of stakeholders," that is, defining who is the strategic target audience for the messages to be sent. In a second moment, came the "mobilization of influencers," an item detailed with a cost of R$ 170,000.00 (one hundred and seventy thousand) within the total project cost of R$ 800,000.00.

One of the 10 items included in the FSB action plan and presented in the contract was the conduct of an opinion poll to verify the popularity of the plan to privatize Eletrobras, with a specific cost of R$ 120,000.00 (one hundred and twenty thousand).

===== PAGE 173 [page-d60726c4320b0e2840158bb3] =====
--- seg-51755ae44a146b633a3b6797 [machine-unreviewed] ---

--- seg-635e301ca9458aa731d2831d [machine-unreviewed] ---

The contract between Eletrobras and FSB also stipulates in item 7.1 that payments between the contracting entity and the contracted party will be made upon the "delivery of the monthly reports prepared by the contracted party corresponding to the consolidation of the achieved results." The report requested these reports through another access to information request law, but although the contract itself was made available through the access to information law, even in a final instance, access to the reports was denied.

A third access to information request was made to Eletrobras regarding information about the alleged bidding process for the relevant contract, ECE-DJS 1252/2017. The request sought the names of the bidders, the proposals, the process documents, and the final result. It was also denied at both the first and second instance.

In the denial, Eletrobras justifies the secrecy regarding the bidding process as part of what it calls "social capital democratization," stating that "it concerns a strategic information of Eletrobras, since the requested documents are directly linked to the company's activities in the competitive market." It continues: "This is because the information regarding the contract with RP Brasil Comunicações (FSB Comunicação) is a fundamental pillar of Eletrobras' social capital democratization process." It also highlights the strategic importance of the contract between Eletrobras and FSB: "Indeed, it is worth noting that the disclosure of information regarding the Contract with RP can be so sensitive that it may cause harm to the so-called democratization process."

The report filed an appeal with the General Control of the Union (CGU), arguing the contradiction between having access to the contract but being denied access to the reports and bidding process, as well as other access to information law issues that guarantee such access. The CGU has not responded yet.

Despite Eletrobras' denial of transparency in the access to the bidding process, the report investigated, through various sources, how the competition unfolded. Or, more accurately, how it did not unfold. At least from a certain point.

In the midst of the Temer government's rush to privatize Eletrobras, a "price taking" was conducted to determine who would win the ECE-DJS 1252/2017 contract. Price taking is a crucial moment in a bidding process where the price threshold for the final auction is determined, and market price parameters are demonstrated. It is also, in a general and generic sense, a moment in the bidding process where prices can be inflated and overcharged.

The book "An Analysis in the Light of the Vulnerabilities of Public Tenders in Brazil" (José Luciano de Oliveira, Descartes Almeida Fontes, Rodrigo Alexandre, and Bruno Andrey) shows that, again in a general sense, "in this phase, various types of fraud can occur, such as bid rigging, pre-agreement, price fixing, overcharging, and the qualification of non-existent companies."

Typically, three budgets from different companies are used. When contracting the services in question, the institution conducts the tender procedures in accordance with specific legislation, and both companies that were budgeted in the price taking phase and any other company can participate, as long as they observe market values. Thus, whenever the price taking stage is won, a tender is held.

The unusual is what happened at Eletrobras regarding the ECE-DJS 1252/2017 contract, according to various sources interviewed by Sportlight Investigative Journalism Agency. The reports, which complement each other, state that some of the country's largest companies in the advisory and communication sector participated in the competition. In addition to FSB, proposals were submitted by Companhia de Noticias (CDN) and Informe Comunicação. The three occupy the podium

According to the investigation by the report, Informe Comunicação presented the proposal with the lowest financial cost, ranking first. FSB came in second. However, after the result of the "price quote" from companies called for a bidding process, the rules changed: Eletrobras decided to choose the winner through the "inexibility" modality, where competition is dispensed and direct contracting is promoted. The law grants the right to the contractor to choose the supplier if there are reasons to justify the dispensation of bidding.
In the relevant contract, Eletrobras argued that "due to its complexity and singularity, as well as confidentiality, involving strategic information of the company, it could only be done through the inapplicability of bidding, which makes it impossible to establish objective criteria, requiring a company with recognized expertise in communication strategy" as stated in Eletrobras' response at the end of the report in "Another Perspective". The other parties involved in the "price quote" have contracts with other entities of the same federal government to develop communication strategies.
On October 17, 2017, almost a month after the signing of the contract between FSB and Eletrobras, the company published the result in the Official Gazette of the Union, announcing the result with FSB as the holder of the contract by "inexibility of bidding".

The behind-the-scenes of the non-competition point to a decisive hand in choosing
after the price taking by "unavailability of bidding" that declared the victory of FSB:
Wilson Pinto Ferreira Junior, appointed by Michel Temer to preside the state-owned company.
Wilson Pinto Ferreira Júnior, 58, took over Eletrobras with a specific mission given by Michel Temer: to lead the privatization process. He started his professional life at the São Paulo Energy Company (CESP) and was promoted to distribution manager of the company during the first term of Mário Covas as governor of São Paulo (1995). In 1998, he moved to the private sector as the first president of Rio Grande Energia, created after the partial privatization of electricity distribution in the state of Rio Grande do Sul by then-governor Antônio Britto. He took over the presidency of the CPFL company in March 2000 and has been presiding the holding since 2002.
The appointment of Wilson Pinto Ferreira Júnior by Michel Temer was on July 22, 2016.

Since Michel Temer took office as president on May 12, 2016, the privatization of Eletrobras has been the government's obsession, which has already issued three Provisional Measures (MP) to facilitate the sale of Eletrobras.

With Temer still serving as interim president, the executive branch issued Provisional Measure (MP) 735, approved by Congress, aiming to facilitate the transfer of control of assets and the privatizations of Eletrobras' distribution companies.

In 2017, MP 814 removed from Law 10.848/2004, which deals with energy commercialization, the article excluding Eletrobras and its controlled companies - Furnas, Companhia

===== PAGE 179 [page-4e6972ebb4a473d01c823389] =====
--- seg-b470942cefdf6ebc3a1d510c [machine-unreviewed] ---

--- seg-35646cba67951ac4eb256280 [machine-unreviewed] ---

--- seg-ab7e841e80ed9679ad4d8ce1 [needs-review] ---
The hydroelectric power plant of São Francisco, Eletronorte, Eletrosul, and the Thermal Electric Generation Company (CGTEE) — part of the National Privatization Program.
The rapporteur of MP 814/2017 is Federal Deputy Júlio Lopes (PP-RJ), former Secretary of Transportation in Rio de Janeiro during the Sérgio Cabral administration, who appears in the reward-based testimony of Benedicto Júnior from Odebrecht, in a denunciation of receiving R$ 15.6 million, as per a spreadsheet delivered to the Federal Public Ministry (MPF-RJ). By the testimony, between 2008 and 2014, the deputy allegedly received 91 payments. The rapporteur of the MP for privatizing Eletrobras is listed in the Odebrecht bribe list by the nicknames "Pavão", "Bonitão", "Bonitinho", "Velho", and "Casa de Doido". Júlio Lopes is also cited in Jacob Barata's, the "Bus King", testimony regarding the receipt of bribes in the scheme of a cash box for politicians from the Federation of Passenger Transportation Companies of the State of Rio de Janeiro (Fetranspor).
Former Deputy Pedro Corrêa cites the rapporteur of MP 814/2017 in his testimony as follows: "This guy needs to be investigated. He made a mess at the Rio de Janeiro secretariat." He also states that, due to "Casa de Doido's" greed, he gave the following advice, both to him and to Eduardo Cunha, who is imprisoned in Operation Carwash: "Look, if you guys who just arrived in Brasília are that thirsty for the pot, you're going to end up being removed from office." Júlio Lopes denies all accusations.
In its propaganda, the government boasts that it will achieve R$ 12.2 billion through privatization, always referred to as "democratization of capital." However, according to the Ministry of Mines and Energy itself, the state-owned company's patrimonial value is R$ 46.2 billion, and the company's total assets reach R$ 170.5 billion. In addition to R$ 541 billion invested since its creation in 1962.
A war of injunctions and in the National Congress has been waged on this topic. To try to win the information battle, Eletrobras launched a communication campaign for the "majority shareholder's project for the company's privatization," which is included in the contract discussed here, the ECE-DJS 1252/2017, from the bidding that ended with FSB. In the newspapers, according to Sportlight Agency's investigative journalism survey, there is a greater diffusion and increase in the tone of negative news about Eletrobras' management and results after signing the contract with FSB.
Column notes, TV comments, constructed agendas to demonstrate the urgent need for privatization, such as in the cases reproduced below. In all communication media. News about how profitable the auction would be, headlines about the losses caused by "obstacles to privatization," daily notes in analysts' columns showing that there is only this path left in light of the state-owned company's numbers.”
In light of this denunciation, I request that this Financial Control and Fiscalization Commission, with the assistance of the Union Accounting Court, carry out a fiscalization and control act regarding this contract, in order to investigate the proper application of the resources.

Mr. President:
I request from Your Excellency, based on Article 50 of the Federal Constitution and in accordance with Articles 115 and 116 of the Internal Regulation, that, after consulting the Desk, information be requested from Mr. State Minister of Transport, Ports and Civil Aviation, in order to clarify this House regarding the problems that occurred on the margins of the highway BR-040 in Petrópolis/RJ, especially regarding actions aimed at ensuring the life, security and housing of the citizens affected by the disaster that occurred in November 2017.
--- seg-69235f53e1bf55979cd34c3f [needs-review] ---
JUSTIFICATION

A landslide caused the formation of a crater on the side of the BR-040 highway, at kilometer 81, heading towards Rio de Janeiro, on November 7, 2017. This event immediately destroyed dozens of homes, others had to be demolished later due to irreparable damage, and over fifty were closed, leaving over a hundred people homeless in the region known as Vale da Escola. A municipal school was also affected, preventing over seventy students from attending classes.

The affected people, even after more than five months, still lack adequate assistance and demand a definitive solution. Despite the initiatives of the Civil Defense of Petrópolis Municipality, the Federal Public Ministry, and the orders of the 4th Civil Court of Petrópolis, the highway concessionaire, Concer, remains inactive regarding the matter and has contributed little to solving the problem.

An inspection report prepared by IBAMA identified that the cause of the incident is related to problems in the construction of a tunnel. According to the report, signs that the structure could collapse were already noticeable long before the event, and the lack of rainfall in the state of Rio de Janeiro was what prevented the collapse from happening earlier.

===== PAGE 181 [page-d2102051061fce3b459dd9d8] =====
--- seg-c76fc25197d0e7b32f007a3d [machine-unreviewed] ---

However, the fact that the work had been halted since the previous year contributed both to the
inability to identify the problem in a timely manner and to the degradation of the already completed parts of the work.
According to the report, continuing the work would prevent water accumulation, which is a determining factor for the collapse.
Even more concerning is the fact that the problem may recur in the same
location if the drainage and containment works recommended in the Technical Report of the Civil Defense Secretariat and Voluntary Actions of the Municipality of Petrópolis are not carried out. Regarding these works, the Federal Public Ministry requested a conciliation hearing in February 2018, aiming to have Concer carry out these actions.
The construction of a new climb up the Petrópolis mountain range was considered the most important
improvement to the BR-040 highway by the Highway Exploration Program, as per the concession contract signed in 1995. However, the start of the works, initially planned for the first year of the concession in 2011, was only effectively executed in 2013 and 2014.
In addition, the implementation cost, estimated at R$ 80 million in April 1995, which
today would correspond, in updated values, to approximately R$ 330 million, jumped to R$ 897 million
after the concessionaire submitted the basic project in 2012, a threefold increase.
In 2015, the National Development Bank - BNDES - approved a loan of R$ 420 million for investments in the aforementioned work.
However, the Federal Public Ministry points out irregularities, on the part of the National Land Transport Agency - ANTT, in the approval of the start of the works regarding requirements provided for in Law No. 8.666/93, the so-called Law of Tenders, and in the release of resources through a contract addendum in violation of the Annual Budget Law of 2014 and the 1988 Federal Constitution.
The Union Accounts Court - TCU - identified, through processo nº 023.204/2015-0 in 2016,
irregularities in the implementation of the concession contract, such as overvaluation of the amount
necessary for economic and financial rebalancing, overpricing in the work budget, and outdated and deficient basic and executive projects.
Administrators of the Triunfo Group - controller of Concer - were recently denounced
by the Public Ministry in Operation Integration, the 48th phase of Lava Jato, which investigates diversions and
frauds in tenders at the Department of Roads and Highways of Paraná.
Thus, the scenario is extremely concerning and the situation of the affected families demands
urgent and definitive solutions. It is not acceptable that citizens have their right to housing restricted due
to successive failures of the Public Administration and the concessionaires to whom public services are granted. In this particular case, we refer to the citizens affected by the incident that occurred on the margins of the BR-040 in Petrópolis, almost six months ago.

--- seg-48e3639e48485197d9de06ab [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-02d9083216338475e4bc7513 [needs-review] ---
Last year, Deputy Cesar Halum addressed a request to the National Telecommunications Agency – ANATEL, Ofício nº 290/2017, through which he forwarded a demand from the City Council of Araguaína/TO, aiming to promote the expansion of access to the Personal Mobile Service – SMP (mobile phone and mobile broadband) to the Novo Horizonte district. He received report No. 45/2017/SEI/PRUV/SPR from that Agency, highlighting the following:

"However, it is worth noting that the mandatory coverage area for mobile telephony, SMP, among the existing obligations, only includes the district seats of municipalities. A municipality is considered covered when the coverage area includes at least 80% (eighty percent) of the urban area of the district seat. Rural coverage reaches any demand for a location situated within 30 (thirty) kilometers of the municipal seat's limit, with fixed voice and data services. The Novo Horizonte locality, in principle, is located less than 30 km from the limits of the district seat of the municipality of Araguaína, and thus is eligible for fixed telephony and fixed internet data services by the provider CLARO, in accordance with the Licensing Tender No. 004/2012/PVCP/SPV – ANATEL.

The provider CLARO declared the coverage of the municipality of Araguaína with the aforementioned services, still subject to this Agency's inspection.

And, furthermore, regarding mobile telephony coverage (2G or 3G technology):

'... Coverage of municipality seats with a population above 100,000 inhabitants with SMP (3G technology) by May 31, 2016'."

It is noteworthy that Araguaína is the second most populous municipality in the State of Tocantins, behind only the capital Palmas, and according to information provided by ANATEL, the Novo Horizonte district should already have mobile telephony coverage, as it is located less than 30 km (thirty kilometers) from the district seat.

In this regard, and considering the documents attached to this Request (offices to ANATEL and CLARO), the information to be provided by the Minister of State for Science, Technology,

(from the Committee on Foreign Affairs and National Defense)
Requests, in accordance with constitutional and parliamentary procedures, that a request for information be sent, through the Speaker of this House, to His Excellency the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Aloysio Nunes Ferreira, regarding the situation of the Brazilian Evangelical Community in Rwanda, particularly the missionaries, following the recent closure of hundreds of evangelical churches and the arrest of Protestant pastors by the government of that country.

Mr. President,

I request, based on Article 50, § 2 of the Federal Constitution, in conjunction with Article 115, I, and 116 of the Internal Regulation of the Chamber of Deputies, that, after consulting the Desk, a request for information be sent to His Excellency, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Aloysio Nunes Ferreira, regarding the situation of the Brazilian Evangelical Community in Rwanda, especially of the missionaries, following the recent closure of hundreds of Evangelical churches and the arrest of Protestant pastors by the government of that country.

JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-823810b2cb39da98416c6498 [machine-unreviewed] ---
In recent days, the media has reported that the Rwandan government has closed hundreds of churches and dozens of mosques. The government has banned over 6,000 churches and around 100 mosques. The majority of the closed churches are Pentecostal.

The government claims that the closed churches and mosques failed to meet safety and noise pollution standards set by Rwandan law. The move followed a catastrophe at a church where 16 worshippers died and 140 were injured after lightning struck the building. According to the government spokesperson, churches and mosques can resume their activities if they meet the standards established by law.

According to the press, the closures are actually aimed at exerting greater control over the growing religious community in the African country3. According to Rwandan President Paul Kagame, the number of religious groups in the country has increased significantly in recent years.
--- seg-7164e26e6cb3cae14b31e7f5 [not-required] ---
3
--- seg-cfd11314c29f56e005b0f4ac [machine-unreviewed] ---
The Washington Post. Rwanda closes thousands of churches in bid for more control. <https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/africa/rwanda-closes-thousands-of-churches-in-bid-for-more- control/2018/04/04/1a758880-37f0-11e8-af3c-2123715f78df_story.html?utm_term=.e238679537a9>

The number of churches and mosques is excessive for a country as small as Rwanda. According to BBC4, six pastors who defied the state order were arrested by the Rwandan police, accused of promoting subversive gatherings.

Human Rights Defenders argue that the closure of churches and mosques follows a government campaign against freedom of expression. A proposal to regulate religious organizations separately from other civil society organizations is pending in the Rwandan Parliament. The proposal is expected to be approved by the Legislative Power, given the government's support from the majority of parliamentarians.

It is in these terms that we request the above information, so that we may know the situation of the Brazilian Evangelical community in Rwanda, particularly the missionaries.

**Inquiries:**
**Regarding Committed Operations and Their Impact on Public Debt**

1) Why has the volume of committed operations grown so much (from 3.2% of the total Gross Government Debt in November 2002 to 24.7% in August 2017)?
2) Why, instead of significantly increasing the balance of committed operations, were these operations not combined with the definitive sale of public titles held by the Central Bank, thereby reducing its stock and contributing to the National Treasury's efforts to lengthen the profile of public debt?
3) Why does the Central Bank hold in its portfolio an amount of public titles exceeding 20% of GDP, while the international average is below 5%?
4) What is the need for the Central Bank to maintain a portfolio with such a high volume of public titles, given that Law No. 11,803 of 2008 provides for the possibility of transferring public titles from the National Treasury to the Central Bank whenever necessary to cover the latter's negative results or to meet monetary policy needs, with prior authorization from the Minister of Finance and without financial counterparty?
5) It is observed that much of the effort conducted by the National Treasury to lengthen the average maturities of public debt and reduce the percentage of papers corrected by the Selic rate has been "annulled" by the increase in the stock of committed operations, which are characterized by extremely short terms and interest rates, although fixed, that express the current Selic rate. How is coordination between the actions of the National Treasury and the Central Bank aimed at improving the profile of public debt?
6) By maintaining a stock of committed operations exceeding R$ 1 trillion, which needs to be constantly renewed, how vulnerable does the Central Bank (and consequently the Brazilian economy) become to a speculative attack by the financial market? Justify.
7) In what way does the separate management of the two essential components (on one side, public titles managed by the National Treasury; on the other, committed operations administered by the Central Bank) compromise the effectiveness of public debt management?
8) Why do committed operations not appear in the Annual Financing Plans (PAFs), an instrument for planning the management of public titles prepared by the National Treasury Secretariat, since they fall within both the scope of Liquid Public Debt (DLSP) and Gross General Government Debt (DBGG)?
9) What should be the limit for the amount of federal mobile debt referred to in Article 48, paragraph XIV of the Constitution?
a. Should this limit be established for gross debt, liquid debt, or both? Justify.

**JUSTIFICATION**

This federal deputy's two Information Requests from the Chamber of Deputies regarding the subject matter at hand—Brazilian citizens' access to classified information concerning the registration and study of unidentified flying objects (UFOs) and their crew, commonly known as ufology—are referenced as:

RIC 
4470/2009 
679/2011

These were partially answered by the three Armed Forces, representing primarily the Ministry of Defense, within what the Forces claim to be the truth reported in their subordinate bodies' archives. These responses confirmed not only the existence of such information but also some incidents involving alleged UFOs and their crew, as well as the seriousness with which at least the Brazilian Air Force (FAB) handles the matter. Today, there are over 10,000 pages of documents and other types of information in various formats, collected in batches and held by the National Archive in Brasília and Rio de Janeiro, all sent by FAB. This does not include the procedures of this Force regarding the collection, registration, archiving, and subsequent retrieval of materials to public archives, outlined in Portaria 551/GC3 of August 9, 2010, published by FAB and known among scholars and specific media as the "ET Law."

Despite the efforts demonstrated by the Brazilian Air Force, many issues raised in previous requests remain unresolved. Over time—it has been seven years since the last RIC's responses—there is no similar willingness from the other forces, the Army and Navy, to provide data to interested citizens, as the same phenomenon that led FAB to adopt and publish its procedures for registration and archiving occurs not only in air space but also over and under Brazilian territorial waters, and its activity is also recorded on land, across the 8.5 million square kilometers of Brazilian territory, making it a matter to be addressed not by one but by all three defense forces of the national territory.

In particular, the justificatory basis for this Request focuses on seeking information about a specific case of significant national impact and worldwide resonance, known in the media as "The Varginha ET Case" or among ufologists as "The Varginha Case," as it occurred in that Minas Gerais city in early 1996 and its press coverage lasted at least another year. This case is of singular importance for several reasons, but two are of paramount importance to scientific knowledge and the transparency of public acts: first, because, according to ufologists, it involves the crash of an unknown-technology UFO and the capture of at least two of its crew, and second, due to the impressive cover-up operation of the facts, for reasons that are not yet fully clear. Suspicions also lead to another serious conclusion, regarding a possible breach of national sovereignty, as the final destination of the crashed ship's materials and captured bodies, according to ufologists, was the United States of America, against the wishes of several officers, for obvious reasons.

The lack of public information about the case, considered true by a large portion of Varginha's population, results in prejudice, ridicule, embarrassment, pain, and doubt among witnesses and relatives of those directly involved, such as the family of military police officer Marco Eli Chereze, who was reportedly a fatal victim of direct contact with one of the crew members.

Under the LAI (Law of Access to Information), which was sanctioned after the aforementioned __UFO_PROTECTED_000__s were answered, new questions about the procedures, especially those of the Army, were raised. Since 2012, several requests have been made to the Federal Government's Electronic Service of Citizen Information (e-SIC), all denied or answered in a way that does not reveal what may remain classified. This is the case, for example, with the strange absence, to date, on the Army's website, of the Document Indexing Codes (CIDICs) containing classified information, originating in 1996 and 1997. According to Article 45, Item II of Decree No. 7,724, one of the decrees that emerged to complement and give effect to the LAI, all documents still classified should have their identifications in code format available on a specific list, on the electronic pages of the public bodies responsible for them, by June 1st of each year. If these documents do indeed exist and were generated between 1996 and 1997, as we are shown by...

already reclassified in the same category, remaining hidden from society until 2046.

On the last day 21/03, parts of Brazil went dark due to a technical issue in the National Interconnected System – SIN, which, as it turned out, was the largest blackout in Brazil's history.

This problem raises a necessary discussion about the process of privatizing the State Electric Sector. Various headlines failed to convey the issue, opening the door to all sorts of speculation, including from the then-mining and energy minister, Fernando Coelho, who, as we know, knows little about the sector; see the news below: Mining and Energy Minister Fernando Coelho Filho stated that the blackout occurred after a failure at the Belo Monte power plant in Pará. The Pará Electric Company (Celpa) reported that a problem with energy generation at the Tucuruí power plant, in the northeast of the state, may have caused the blackout. (g1.globo.com - 21/03/2018 4:56 pm)

According to information from industry representatives, the problem occurred at the Xingu Substation, at the output of the CC bipolar of the Belo Monte Transmissora de Energia - BMTE, which, contrary to what was initially reported, does not belong to Eletronorte and is not in Tucuruí.

As it turned out, during testing on the transmission line carrying 4GW of load, a failure occurred, causing the line to go offline, triggering a chain reaction. According to the National Operator of the Electric System (ONS), on page At 3:48 pm on 21/03/2018, a circuit breaker failed at the Xingu Substation in Pará. Consequently, several 500 kV transmission lines, components of the North/Northeast/Central-West interconnection trunks, Tucuruí/Manaus, Tucuruí/Vila do Conde, 800 kV Xingu/Estreito and the UTE Belo Monte, among others, were automatically shut down, resulting in a total load reduction in the SIN of 18,000 MW.

As seen, the state-owned company Eletronorte had no responsibility for the problem, as the Xingu Substation is operated and maintained by the Xingu Transmissora de Energia Lines (controlled by the Spanish group Isolux). The LT (CC) +-800kV Xingu/Estreito is under the responsibility of BMTE (which built or is building a converter station at the Xingu Substation), BMTE is a concessionaire of the State Grid group that wants to buy Eletrobras.

In light of this, we question the Ministry of Mines and Energy and the National Operator of the Electric System:

1. What was the extent of the incident?
2. What were the causes of the blackout?
3. Was the company conducting tests on the equipment at that time?
4. ...
5. ...
6. ...
7. ...
8. ...
9. ...

What were the losses caused by the blackout in the affected cities?
How long did the blackout last and how long did it take for the system to return to normal?
Was an investigation initiated by ONS? Has it been completed? What is the result of the investigation?
Which company is responsible for substation Xingu? What is the date of the concession?

Mr. President:

I request, based on Article 50 of the Federal Constitution and in accordance with Articles 115 and 116 of the Internal Regulation, that, after consulting the Desk, information be requested from the Minister of State for Finance in order to inform this House on the following points:

1) What is the amount of federal tax and social security debts, registered in the Union's Active Debt, and processes with values above R$15,000,000.00 (fifteen million reais)?

2) How many taxpayers are in this situation? Divided by states and regions? With a focus on the 100 highest values.

JUSTIFICATION

The tax transaction is a mechanism provided for in Article 156, paragraph III, of the National Tax Code.

However, there has never been a federal law regulating the matter.

On the other hand, a bill (Project of Law No. 5.082/2009) is currently being discussed in this House, proposed by the Executive Branch, which aims to regulate the tax transaction of debts managed by the General Prosecution of the National Treasury.

In our view, the tax transaction can be a fair and equitable way to resolve tax impasses between the Treasury and taxpayers. However, data must be presented regarding the viability and financial advantage of the measure.

For these reasons, we request the above information.

Chamber of Sessions, May 3, 2018.

JUSTIFICATION
An attached draft law, of my authorship, aims to readjust the monthly progressive tax table values
for Individual Income Tax, as well as the exempt portion for pensions, retirement, remunerated leave,
and retirement for those over 65, the deductions for dependents with educational expenses,
and the maximum simplified deduction value.
--- seg-e1c571375bb07ff52803e8dd [needs-review] ---
The initiative, if approved, will result in a change in the Union's tax revenue, and as such, its
processing must be subject to the command of Article 114 of the Budgetary Guidelines Law, as follows:
"Article 114. Only will be approved the bill project or edited the provisional measure that
institutes or alters public revenue when accompanied by the corresponding demonstration
of the estimate of the impact on the collection, duly justified"
Thus, in order to comply with the requirements contained in the aforementioned legislation and
allow the bill project to be processed in the National Congress, it is essential to forward
this request to the competent bodies of the federal tax administration.

JUSTIFICATION
PL 8.803/2017 aims to define the concept of pets and establish norms for the
smooth functioning of the productive chain, which will be conceptualized as industry (veterinary
products, food, and advice), services and trade (hotels, clinics, and pet shops), and breeding,
as well as to resolve the conflict issues established by Law Complementary No. 140/11,
where, in addition to violating the principles of free initiative and economic order, some Federal
Entities invade the constitutional material competence reserved for the Union.

for the use of animals in research.

===== PAGE 225 [page-2e79644b6f214bfaa986ca27] =====
--- seg-bcb20f3a177ae11193bea633 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018
--- seg-e625168e0328e58525b5c706 [machine-unreviewed] ---

--- seg-ce8f3107a5299a7e62bc5b57 [needs-review] ---
In August 2017, the Presidency decided, in accordance with Article 34, II, of the Internal Regulation,
to establish a Special Commission to provide a report on Senate Federal Project of Law No. 6,814, 2017,
which "establishes rules for public procurement and contracts and repeals Law No. 8,666 of June 21, 1993,
Law No. 10,520 of July 17, 2002, and provisions of Law No. 12,462 of August 4, 2011." At that time,
Project of Law No. 7,228, 2017, which "regulates Article 37, XXI of the Federal Constitution to establish
general norms for the conduct of public procurement and the conclusion of contracts in the Union,
states, Federal District and municipalities, and provides for other measures," was already appended to
the aforementioned bill. Both proposals share the common goal of providing new regulation for
Article 37, XXI of the Constitution and promoting significant changes to the rules on public
procurement and contracts.

Subsequently, in February of this year, the members were designated and the Commission was
established, becoming known in this House as the New Public Procurement Law Commission.
However, after the Commission's deliberative meetings began, the Presiding Officer granted a
request made by Dep. José Guimarães to append Bills of Law No. 6,814, 2017 and No. 7,228, 2017
to Bill of Law No. 1,292, 1995 and change the Commission's name as follows:

Append Bill of Law No. 6.814/2017 to Bill of Law No. 1.292/1995.
Accordingly, revise the initial dispatch on Bill of Law No. 1.292/1995 to include
an examination by the Commission on Environment and Sustainable Development and the
Commission on Economic Development, Industry, Trade and Services.

Furthermore, change the name of the Special Commission for Bill of Law No. 6.814/2017
to refer to Bill of Law No. 1.292/1995, which will lead the block under review.
--- seg-ab802a18713e7c1c2aa9f940 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Publish.
--- seg-1ba3a3e6c057dcdabd217bed [machine-unreviewed] ---
Office
--- seg-d6208575f5b76c50fdb89a0b [needs-review] ---
However, the simultaneous processing of the proposals reveals itself to be inappropriate and does not meet the procedural assumptions. Indeed, as decided in Order Question No. 640, 2010, the Special Commissions provided for in Article 34, II, of the RICD "are established with the specific purpose of issuing a report on a particular proposal or set of proposals appended to it, due to the matter contained in the legislative initiative, and it is not within the competence of these bodies to examine other proposals, besides that for which they were created."

The decision further added that allowing the appendage of other proposals "would constitute a measure tending to perpetuate the functioning of a Special Commission, which is not compatible with its nature as a Temporary Commission, as classified in Article 33 of the RICD."

The risk of becoming permanent is exactly what occurs in the present case. In fact, PL No. 1,292, 1995, has 223 other proposals appended to it, and the simultaneous processing of the matters may become a significant obstacle to this Legislative House's proper consideration of the relevant and urgent content of the New Procurement Law proposed by PL No. 6,814, 2017, so eagerly awaited by all involved sectors.

===== PAGE 226 [page-23a25ae99310143d60f159c1] =====
--- seg-6299a9145591292e8b4b26f0 [machine-unreviewed] ---
226 Tuesday 15
--- seg-07170e2ca4e590542769e8e1 [machine-unreviewed] ---
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES
--- seg-ef3c65bc61f142b3208c61ec [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018
--- seg-bcfb549d136d1deb1de88d11 [needs-review] ---
See, on the other hand, that PL No. 1,292 of 1995 and its 223 appended projects address specific issues within the generic theme of procurement contracts and aim to amend specific provisions of the existing legislation.

Thus, the object and scope of the proposals are different: while PL No. 1,292 of 1995 and its other appended projects seek to alter specific points of norms on procurement, PL No. 6,814 of 2017 presents a New Law on Procurement and Contracts, replacing the three main existing norms on the subject – namely, Law No. 8,666 of 1993 (Procurement Law), Law No. 10,520 of 2002 (Auction Law), and Law No. 12,462 of 2012 (Differentiated Contract Regime) – with a single, complete norm, which will also bring important innovations, such as the possibility of resolving conflicts through arbitration and conciliation.

Therefore, the mere fact that they have as a connecting element the reference to the generic term of public procurement and contracts should not, in itself, lead to the joint processing of the proposals.

At this point, it is necessary to clarify that the Board of the Chamber of Deputies has already authorized requests for disassociation in similar situations, such as the acceptance of Request No. 4,763 of 2012.

The disassociation of PLs No. 6,814 of 2017 and No. 7,228 of 2017 will also ensure the much-needed speed in the processing of the matter, especially in this year when it will be necessary for parliamentarians to also dedicate their efforts to the elections.

For these reasons, supported by what was decided by the Presidency in Order Question No. 640 of 2010, as well as by Request No. 4,763 of 2012, I request that the disassociation of the Projects of Law No. 6,814 and 7,228 of 2017, and Project of Law No. 1,292 of 1995, be determined, renaming the committee to Special Commission designated to issue a report on Project of Law No. 6,814 of 2017.

I request from Your Excellency, in accordance with Article 52, § 6, of the Internal Regulation of this House, the
forwarding of Legislative Decree Project No. 578/2016, from the Federal Senate - which "suspends Article 13 of Resolution No.
400, of December 13, 2016, from the National Civil Aviation Agency - Anac" - to the next standing committee as noted in the attached dispatch, or alternatively, to the Plenum, since the Committee on Transportation and Communications did not complete its review of the matter within the additional deadlines, each of 10 sessions, granted by the House President in a decision on the two previously submitted requests.

The aforementioned project, which aims to prevent the charging of checked baggage surcharges, authorized by the National Civil Aviation Agency - Anac in December 2016, has been the subject of unanimous criticism from consumer protection agencies and entities, as well as representatives of the Public Ministry, and has even been the subject of a judicial decision in a preliminary injunction.

JUSTIFICATION

The opinion on PDC 578/2016 was approved by the Consumer Defense Committee on June 13, 2017, and the proposal was received by the Committee on Transportation and Communications the following day, June 14, 2017. However, that Committee, after the regulatory deadline of 40 sessions as stipulated in the Internal Regulation to issue a statement on the matter, had this deadline extended by an additional 10 sessions, by concession of the House President, which began on November 13, 2017, as a result of Request No. 7.615/2017, presented by this member on November 6, 2017, while I was presiding over the Consumer Defense Committee.

Upon the expiration of the additional deadline without the Committee completing its review, a new Redistribution Request No. 7.879/2017 was submitted on December 8, 2017, requesting the forwarding of the matter to the subsequent Committee or to the Plenum.

However, on December 18, 2017, in response to Request No. 7.879/2017, the President granted an additional 10-session deadline for the Committee on Transportation and Communications to issue its opinion on the project.

It is worth noting that on March 23, 2018, Your Excellency denied Request No. 8220/2018, submitted by Deputy Ronaldo Carletto (PP-BA).

We have also verified that, with one session remaining until the expiration of the last deadline granted by Your Excellency to the CVT, the Rapporteur, Deputy Milton Monti, returned the matter without a committee opinion to the commission secretariat.

The harm to consumers is evident and there has undoubtedly been an increase in fares, which, according to a Foundation Getúlio Vargas study, reached 35.9%. According to IBGE data, however, the increase was more moderate, at 16.9%, even though the companies had committed to this Parliament that the measure would reduce ticket prices.

JUSTIFICATION
The bill 6989/2017, of my authorship, which amends the Civil Marco of the Internet, Law No. 12.965 of April 23, 2014, to include a procedure for the removal of content that induces, incites, or assists suicide through internet applications, has a request for inclusion in the agenda (REQ. 6344/2017) and urgency (REQ. 6318/2017).

BILL NO. 1,145-A, 2011
(From Mr. Carlos Bezerra)
Adds article 392-B to the Consolidation of Labor Laws to provide for maternity leave for
women working on crews of merchant marine vessels, river and lake navigation, port traffic, and fishing
vessels; with the opinion of the Commission on Women's Rights, for approval with an amendment (relator:
DEP. ANA PERUGINI).
NEW DISPATCH:
TO THE COMMITTEES ON:
WOMEN'S RIGHTS;
SOCIAL SECURITY AND FAMILY; AND
CONSTITUTION, JUSTICE, AND CITIZENSHIP (ART. 54 OF RICD) -
CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Conclusive Consideration by the Committees - Art. 24 II
PUBLICATION OF THE OPINION OF
THE COMMISSION ON WOMEN'S RIGHTS
I - REPORT
The distinguished Deputy Carlos Bezerra presented to the House the aforementioned proposal
aiming to grant 180 days of maternity leave to employees working on crews of vessels.
The bill adds an article 392-B to the Consolidation of Labor Laws to grant the benefit to
pregnant women working on crews of merchant marine, river, lake, and port traffic vessels, as well as
fishing vessels.
The leave can occur at any time, starting from 70 days before the expected delivery. Rest
periods before and after the delivery can be extended by two weeks, depending on the presentation of a
medical certificate to the employer.
The proposal also ensures that the employee can be transferred to a different job when health
conditions require it; and that she can return to her previous job with a salary equivalent to the average
of the wages received in the six months prior to conception, and be dispensed from work for the time
necessary to attend at least six medical consultations and other complementary examinations.
No amendments were presented within the regulatory timeframe.
This is the report.

===== PAGE 240 [page-07ee2dea193b6c2a3c5e0fed] =====
--- seg-874738a731219a8f723d070a [machine-unreviewed] ---

--- seg-98e49ad9e64accd2dbfaf840 [machine-unreviewed] ---

--- seg-c7d25876ea7091c521e6fa36 [machine-unreviewed] ---

--- seg-56c2889fb09767269c31bd72 [machine-unreviewed] ---
II - RELATOR'S VOTE
Article 392 of the CLT, currently in force, reads as follows:

Art. 392. A pregnant employee is entitled to 120 (one hundred and twenty) days of maternity leave, without prejudice to her employment and salary.

§ 1. The employee must, through a medical certificate, notify her employer of the date of the beginning of her absence from work, which may occur between the 28th (twenty-eighth) day before the delivery and the occurrence of the delivery.

§ 2. The rest periods, before and after the delivery, may be extended by 2 (two) weeks each, through a medical certificate.

§ 3. In case of premature delivery, the woman is entitled to the 120 (one hundred and twenty) days provided for in this article.

§ 4. During pregnancy, it is guaranteed to the employee, without prejudice to her salary and other rights:

I - Transfer of duties, when health conditions require it, ensuring the resumption of the previously performed duties immediately after returning to work (Paragraph added by Law No. 9,799 of 5/26/1999);

II - Waiver of working hours for the time necessary to attend at least six medical consultations and other complementary examinations.

§ 5. (VETTED)
--- seg-595b50195c291fe4a8715a5d [needs-review] ---
It is verified that the initiative of the honorable Deputy Carlos Bezerra innovates labor legislation in favor of the onboard employee, extending the maternity leave period from 120 to 180 days. Other modifications such as work leave starting from the 70th day and the guarantee of the 180-day period in case of early termination are adaptations to the proposed total leave period extension.

Extending the maternity leave period to 180 days, as mentioned in the bill, is justified by the special working conditions of these employees. As the author informs us, "the job requires long displacements and constant exposure to dangers, and often ships remain distant from locations with adequate medical assistance." The author's statement is a notory fact and does not require additional demonstrations or suggest controversies. Therefore, the differentiated treatment for those working under special conditions in relation to the group of workers of the same category or similar is justified. The proposed measure is in full accordance with the principles already enshrined in Article 392 of the CLT (Brazilian Labor Code) regarding the protection of motherhood, family, and child.

Another innovation present in the text of the bill refers to the guarantee of equivalent remuneration to the average of the salaries received in the six months prior to conception, in case of transfer.

Regarding the function during pregnancy. However, this point is difficult to understand, as the text states that the
average must be calculated using conception as a reference. If the transfer of function occurred during pregnancy, the
wage average to be paid cannot be based on childbirth, which had not yet occurred. Nevertheless, we only register our
difficulty in reading the proposal at this specific point, as the Commission on Labor, Administration, and Public Service
(CTASP) will undoubtedly conduct a more thorough analysis of the text to reconcile it with the entire labor legislation.

In the substance that this Commission is responsible for analyzing, we understand that the proposal has great social value
and enshrines the principles of protecting motherhood and women's work. And in line with the idea proposed by the bill,
we suggest an amendment to include fixed platforms in the text. The concept of the law does not encompass such vessels,
only those being towed. Thus, if the platform is fixed, the workers who perform their work there will not be included in this
noble proposal.

In light of the above, we advocate for the approval of House Bill No. 1,145, of 2011, with the attached amendment.

BILL NO. 2,083-B, 2011
(From Mr. Manato)
Provides for the mandatory installation of breastfeeding support rooms in federal public agencies and entities, and takes other measures; having received the opinion: of the Commission on the Defense of Women's Rights, for approval with a substitute (rapporteur: DEP. ANA PERUGINI); and of the Commission on Labor, Administration, and Public Service, for approval (rapporteur: DEP. FLÁVIA MORAIS)
--- seg-45b30ccb93117be3bc6cf379 [machine-unreviewed] ---

--- seg-1d52149dad35b2621704d20f [needs-review] ---
PUBLICATION OF THE OPINION OF
THE COMMISSION ON WOMEN'S RIGHTS
I - REPORT
The proposed legislation directs federal public administration bodies and entities to establish breastfeeding support rooms within their premises, allowing lactating servants adequate conditions for milking and storing their milk during working hours.
According to the proposal, breastfeeding support rooms should be installed in an appropriate area, equipped with necessary tools and technical assistance, in accordance with Resolution RDC/Anvisa No. 171 of September 4, 2006, and the Joint Technical Note SAS/MS-ANVISA, drafted based on the aforementioned resolution.
The deadline for the new law to come into effect is 180 days from the date of its publication.
The bill was distributed for merit review to the Commission on Labor, Administration, and Public Service - CTASP, which has already approved it, to this committee, and to the Commission on Social Security and Family - CSSF.
Subsequently, the Commission on Constitution, Justice, and Citizenship - CCJC will need to issue a statement on its constitutionality, juridical validity, and legislative technique.
No amendments were offered to the proposal.

II - VOTE OF THE REPORTER

===== PAGE 244 [page-722373ff02d52428f84df1df] =====
--- seg-494b9a2c2931a990e8155b45 [machine-unreviewed] ---

--- seg-909408eb3842a2660700a86a [machine-unreviewed] ---

Known. On this topic, the Ministry of Health states:
“Breastfeeding is the most wise natural strategy of bond, affection, protection, and
nutrition for the child, and it constitutes the most sensitive, economic, and effective intervention for
reducing child morbidity and mortality. It also has a tremendous impact on promoting the
integral health of the mother-baby duo and brings joy to society as a whole.
..........................................................................................
Breastfeeding is much more than just nourishing the child. It is a process that involves deep
interaction between mother and child, with repercussions on the child's nutritional status, its ability to
defend itself from infections, its physiology, and its cognitive and emotional development, as well as its
long-term health, and it has implications for the mother's physical and mental health.”1
The World Health Organization and the Ministry of Health recommend breastfeeding for
two years or more, with exclusive breastfeeding in the first six months.
In the initial six months, servants have legally assured maternity leave. After that, there are no
legal tools to support servants who wish to continue breastfeeding.
As well noted in the justification of the proposal, women who breastfeed and are away
from their children due to work need to empty their breasts during the daily work schedule for relief from
discomfort and to maintain milk production. However, for milk to be extracted during work hours, the
woman must have a suitable place to do the milking and store the milk. In most cases, this place is not
available.
Therefore, it is timely to discuss the requirement for the installation of breastfeeding
rooms in federal public institutions. It is worth noting that this is a provision of easy implementation and low
cost, as the necessary furniture and equipment basically consist of a chair for milking, a sink, and a
freezer. In some cases, public agencies and entities will only need to relocate these equipment to an
appropriate location.
With a quiet and properly equipped environment, women who wish to continue
breastfeeding can milk their own milk and store it during work hours. At the end of the work day, they can
take the collected milk to their child or even donate it to a milk bank.
However, we understand that, in respect of the principle of equality and as a measure of
justice, the current bill should have its scope expanded to ensure this breastfeeding support structure to
women who work in the private initiative, as well as to state and municipal servants, which is why we
decided to present a substitute.
We also reserve what the rapporteur of the matter in CTASP already pointed out regarding
1 Child Health Care Manual - Breastfeeding and Complementary Feeding - 2015.

**Substitute for House Bill No. 2,083, of 2011**

It establishes the obligation for private institutions and public agencies to install appropriate rooms for breastfeeding women.

**Article 1**

This Law establishes the obligation for private institutions and public agencies to install suitable rooms for breastfeeding women.

**Article 2**

Public agencies that employ or house female servants must install rooms for breastfeeding support to allow for the expression and storage of breast milk during working hours.

**Sole Paragraph**

The obligation stated in the main clause also applies to private institutions that employ female workers.

**Article 3**

The breastfeeding support rooms referred to in Article 2 must be installed in an appropriate area, equipped with necessary equipment and adequate assistance, in accordance with the Joint Technical Note SAS/MS-ANVISA, based on ANVISA Resolution RDC No. 171 of September 4, 2006.

**Article 4**

This Law enters into force 180 days after its official publication.

Commission Chamber, August 21, 2017.

Depute ANA PERUGINI
Reporter

BILL NO. 3.613-A, 2012
(From Mr. Sibá Machado)
Adds a paragraph to Article 12 of Law No. 8,177, of March 1, 1991, which "establishes rules for the
deregulation of the economy and provides for other measures", to determine that savings accounts with
balances exceeding fifty thousand reais (R$ 50,000) shall be remunerated at a percentage of the Selic
reference rate; with the Finance and Taxation Committee's opinion that the matter does not imply an
increase or decrease in public revenue or expenditure, and no opinion on the financial and budgetary
appropriateness; and, on the merits, recommending rejection (report by Dep. Simone Morgado).

DISPOSITION:
TO THE COMMITTEES ON:
FINANCE AND TAXATION (MERIT AND ART. 54, RICD) AND CONSTITUTION AND CITIZENRY (ART. 54 RICD)

CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Conclusive Consideration by the Committees - Art. 24 II
--- seg-714b549425f24bc7e16527cb [needs-review] ---
**PUBLICATION OF THE COMMITTEE ON FINANCE AND TAXATION'S OPINION**

**I - REPORT**

House Bill No. 3,613 of 2012 adds paragraph 5 to Article 12 of Law No. 8,177 of 1991, stipulating that savings accounts with balances exceeding R$ 50,000 shall be remunerated exclusively by a fee corresponding to eighty percent of the interest rate equivalent to the SELIC rate, applied to deposits made effective upon the entry into force of the law derived from the approval of the proposal.

The author of the proposal noted in his justification that, under the legislation in force at the time the matter was presented, deposits were remunerated at a fixed monthly interest rate of 0.5% - equivalent to 6.17% annually - applied to updated values by the TR. At that time, an undesirable asymmetry existed between the remuneration of the savings account and other investments. The returns from savings, coupled with other benefits of this investment mode, made it more attractive, leading to massive transfers of resources and causing enormous distortions in the credit supply.

Proposing a remuneration rate equivalent to eighty percent of the SELIC rate would thus, according to the proposer, allow for greater balance between different types of investments and institutions, protecting small savers from the proposed changes.

The matter, subject to the conclusive consideration of the Committees and in ordinary procedure, should be examined by this Committee regarding aspects related to budgetary and financial compatibility and adequacy, and on the merits, as no amendments were presented. It will then be forwarded to the Committee on Constitution and Legal Affairs.

No amendments were offered within the regulatory deadline.

This is the report.

II - RELATOR'S VOTE

It is this Commission's preliminary task, upon examining the merits, to assess the present proposal regarding its compatibility or appropriateness with the multi-annual plan, the Budget Guidelines Law, and the annual budget, in accordance with the Internal Rules of the Chamber of Deputies (RI, art. 53, II).

The draft law proposes that savings deposits with balances exceeding R$ 50,000 be remunerated exclusively by a fee corresponding to 80% of the interest equivalent to the Selic reference rate. The matter addressed in the draft law has no impact on the Union Budget, as it is essentially normative in character, with no direct impact on public revenue or expenditure.

Regarding the merits, the situation is quite different, given the inconveniences of approving the measure contained in the draft law for the reasons outlined below. Furthermore, we consider that at this moment, the approval of this draft law would imply a disregard for principles that should guide the legal order, as well as action on the part of lawmakers and regulatory bodies.

The proposal introduces changes to the rules governing savings1, with the aim of encouraging the saver (with a savings balance exceeding R$ 50,000) to consider other types of investments, such as those backed by public debt securities, among others.

It is worth noting that one month after the presentation of the draft law in question, the Executive Branch issued MP No. 567, of May 3, 2012, converted into Law No. 12,703, of August 7, 2012. The current legislation establishes that savings deposit balances will be remunerated by the TR plus 70% of the Selic target, as long as the Selic rate does not exceed 8.5% per annum. In practice, the savings account, which previously had a monthly valuation of 0.5% plus the Reference Rate (TR), now renders 70% of Selic plus TR. When Selic exceeds 8.5% per annum, the remuneration of savings returns to TR plus 0.5% per month2.

The formula above contemplates a proportion between the remuneration of savings and the Selic rate, at least up to a certain amount. This provides the necessary market equilibrium for other fixed-income securities, by reducing the risk of capital flight from other investments, including public debt securities issued by the National Treasury, which are equally important for the financial market and the financing of investments in the country.

This decision is particularly significant because the current economic scenario, regarding the trajectory of the basic interest rate, currently at 8.25% per annum, is quickly approaching the conditions observed at the time the matter was presented, when the interest rate was 7.25% per annum.
--- seg-e5fba24722745f3bd7e863a5 [needs-review] ---
1 Investing in savings still remains the preference of 76% of Brazilians, according to a survey by the Federation of Commerce of
--- seg-a91bb7e5f25f3fa885a4f016 [needs-review] ---
in the state of Rio de Janeiro in 2016.
It seems that this preference is explained because it is very easy to make applications and redemptions through it, not to mention that the modality
offers low risk and tax-free financial returns, in addition to protection by the Credit Guarantee Fund (FGC).
2 The savings rule changed with the issuance of MP No. 567, of May 3, 2012, when the savings interest rates were at 9% and
the government of Dilma Rousseff intended to lower them even further. At the time, without the changes made to savings, the drop
could compromise the issuance of public securities by the National Treasury, which are used as loans for the government, as well
as other fixed-income investments.

===== PAGE 249 [page-861c11d41d5ee6b1ab5d1171] =====
--- seg-40c2ccd406629418e1bcbbf9 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018
--- seg-b10d51647b81c80fb55d23e4 [machine-unreviewed] ---

Tuesday 15 249
--- seg-bd3231d0ef01472ebb35b7da [needs-review] ---
In this scenario, with each 1 percentage point cut in the economy's benchmark interest rate, the Selic, the Monetary Policy Committee (COPOM) triggers the savings account profitability trigger, which then pays lower returns whenever Selic is equal to or below 8.5%.

Financial market experts also argue that the savings account interest rate should track the movement of the benchmark interest rate, even if paying lower returns due to its lower risk compared to government bonds, and because its returns are exempt from income tax and financial operations tax, and it is protected by the Credit Guarantee Fund (FGC).

On the other hand, since savings accounts previously had a fixed profitability that did not keep pace with interest rate cuts, even in a context of consistent interest rate reduction, as we are witnessing with the retention of the formula prior to Law No. 12.703 of 2012, the application in savings deposit accounts would become very attractive compared to other fixed-income investment alternatives, such as bank deposit certificates (CDB) and investment funds, potentially leading to a significant increase in the flow of resources to this modality. The insensitivity of savings account profitability to lower interest rates would impose a nearly unbearable burden on homeowners loan borrowers, who would not see their rates reduced, even in a scenario where the economy's benchmark rate is on a downward trajectory.

Therefore, considering the scenario of reduced net savings captations, which leads to reduced amounts allocated to residential financing, the potential approval of the Bill, which only provides for 80% of the benchmark interest rate for savings, in a context where Selic is expected to remain around 7% per annum in the coming months, could bring even worse performance for savings compared to the rule established by Law No. 12.703/2012, potentially causing losses in the real estate market.

In conclusion, in our view, the 2012 Bill No. 3.613 is no longer appropriate for the current economic situation. The motivation that guided its presentation is no longer valid in light of the subsequent approval of Law No. 12.703 of 2012, which found a more balanced formula for those who invest their resources in savings accounts, for economic agents operating in the real estate market, and not least, for borrowers in the housing finance system.

In light of the above, we vote against the implication of the proposal in a decrease in revenue or an increase in public expenditure, and it is not appropriate to comment on its financial and budgetary adequacy. On the merits, we vote against Bill No. 3.613 of 2012.

Chamber of the Committee, November 1, 2017.

Establishes the obligation to identify donations made to natural persons; having the opinion of the

(relator: DEP. JOÃO PAULO KLEINÜBING).
DISPOSITION:

--- seg-0347143f34107b3229efdd40 [needs-review] ---
**PUBLICATION OF THE FINANCE AND TAX COMMITTEE'S OPINION**

**I - REPORT**

House Bill No. 7,171, 2014, authored by Honorable Deputy Mendonça Filho, addresses the
identification of monetary donations and contributions made to natural persons in campaigns of any nature or purpose, excluding electoral campaigns.

From reading the justification of the proposal, it becomes evident that the concern lies with the fact that “the
patria's legal framework allows for monetary donations to be made in campaigns of any nature or purpose without
the need for donor identification, thus hindering any form of state control and, in particular, tax authority
oversight.”

To fulfill the objective of enabling the precise identification of the parties and elements of donations, the
proposal, in Article 2, mandates the opening of a specific bank account for recording donations made to the
beneficiary, as well as the obligation for banks to identify the donor in the respective current account statements,
annotating the registration number in the Individual Taxpayer's Register (CPF) or the National Legal Entity
Register (CNPJ), as applicable.

Furthermore, the sole paragraph of Article 2 stipulates that the aforementioned statement, upon request,
must be made available without judicial authorization.

In turn, Article 3 of the proposal establishes the possibility of utilizing a mechanism available on a dedicated
website that allows for credit card usage to receive the donations and contributions mentioned in Article 1.
According to this provision, donations must meet two requirements listed in the incises: identification of the
debtor as per Article 2 and the issuance of a receipt for each donation made.

II - VOTE OF THE REPORTER
In accordance with article 32, X, “h” of the Internal Regulation of the Chamber of Deputies, this
Committee is responsible for examining the “financial and budgetary aspects of any proposals that result
in an increase or decrease in public revenue or expenditure, as regards their compatibility or
appropriateness with the multi-annual plan, the budget guidelines law, and the annual budget.”
--- seg-8ed03f83e18392e613e60254 [needs-review] ---
The project under review regulates the procedures applicable to donations and contributions made to natural persons, excluding those of an electoral nature. The matter addressed therein is confined to establishing the criteria to be followed by the beneficiary and the donor to ensure greater transparency for these operations. As the author of the proposal states in his justification, the initiative aims to inhibit illegal donations that could fraud the tax system or enable dubious operations, providing constituted powers with new control instruments.

As for the merits, following the opinion previously presented to this Commission by Deputy Edmar Arruda, we initially note that donations constitute a tax-generating fact of state competence, the Inheritance and Donation Tax on Goods or Rights (ITCMD), and thus, states can provide for the submission of information regarding such operations to the competent authorities. Furthermore, the donor, in his income tax declaration, a federal tax, must inform the Federal Revenue about any potential patrimonial increases resulting from a donation.

However, as Deputy Edmar Arruda himself reminded, it is possible that these main and accessory tax obligations are not met, making it relevant to initiate efforts to establish new forms of donation control.

That, in our view, justifies the matter being addressed in other legal spheres beyond the tax one. Mechanisms need to be created to ensure the monitoring of donations made to campaigns. Furthermore, I emphasize that the approval of the bill under review will fill a normative gap. As the Civil Code allows for donations without specifying the use of the donated funds, campaigns could be financed in an unclear manner through these so-called "donations without charge." In other words, someone who wants to donate to a specific campaign could use the "donation without charge" figure to implicitly link the donated resources to the campaign, without explicitly stating their intentions.

The approval of a law establishing stricter rules for donations linked to campaigns of any kind fills this gap and facilitates the oversight of such donations.

For these reasons, we voted in favor of the budgetary and financial adequacy of Law Project No. 7,171, of 2014; and, on the merits, for its approval.

I – REPORT

Bill No. 3.446, 2015, proposes to amend Law No. 7.827 of September 27, 1989, to establish that the Constitutional Funds of the North (FNO), Northeast (FNE), and Central-West (FCO) must allocate at least 20% of their total resources to productive activities of mini and small rural producers and micro and small businesses.

The proposal was distributed for consideration by the Committees on National Integration, Regional Development and the Amazon (merit); Agriculture, Livestock, Supply and Rural Development (merit); Finance and Taxation (article 54 of RICD); and Constitution and Justice and Citizenship (article 54 of RICD).

The Committee on National Integration, Regional Development and the Amazon approved Bill No. 3.446/2015 unanimously on May 24, 2016, in line with the Report of the Rapporteur, Deputy Alan Rick. In turn, the Committee on Agriculture, Livestock, Supply and Rural Development voted against the bill on October 5, 2016, in accordance with the Report of the Rapporteur, Deputy Raimundo Gomes de Matos.

Referred to this Committee on Finance and Taxation, the matter will be analyzed in terms of its appropriateness and budgetary and financial compatibility (article 54 RICD).

II - VOTE
It is up to this Committee to assess the proposal regarding its compatibility or appropriateness with the
multi-annual plan, the Budget Guidelines Act, and the annual budget, in accordance with the Rules of the
Chamber of Deputies (RI, art. 53, II) and the Internal Norms of the Commission on Finance and Taxation of
May 29, 1996, which establishes procedures for examining budget and financial compatibility or
appropriateness.
According to the Rules, only proposals that "entail an increase or decrease in public revenue or
expenditure" are subject to examination of financial and budget compatibility or appropriateness. This is
also stipulated in Article 9 of the Internal Norms approved by CFT on 29.05.96, which states:
"Article 9. When the matter does not have budget and financial implications, the final vote should
conclude that it is not within the Committee's scope to determine whether the proposal is appropriate or
not."
As previously mentioned, PL No. 3.446/2015 proposes to amend Law No. 7.827/1989 to
establish that the Constitutional Funds FNO, FNE, and FCO should allocate at least 20% of their total
resources to productive activities of small and mini rural producers and micro and small enterprises.
From the perspective of budget and financial appropriateness, it can be stated that setting a minimum
percentage (20%) for the application of the total resources of FNO, FNE, and FCO to productive
activities of small and mini rural producers and micro and small enterprises will not in itself result in an
increase in the expenditure provisions for these Funds.
Therefore, upon analyzing PL No. 3.446/2015, we find that its approval would not affect
federal public expenditures, as it would not add to the overall volume of resources allocated to these
Funds and, consequently, to the total expenses projected in the Annual Budget Law.
In light of the above, I vote against the proposal implying an increase or decrease in public
revenue or expenditure of the Law Project No. 3.446, of 2015, and it is not appropriate to make a
pronouncement on its financial and budget appropriateness.
